4G|M8001C0.Description: This counter provides the minimum retention period for a PDCP SDU (DL) inside the eNB. Retention delay is measured for each PDCP SDU. The measurement starts at the reception of a PDCP SDU on PDCP layer and ends at the first TB transmission on MAC layer including the PDCP SDU or the first segment of it.   Note: The PDCP, RLC, MAC protocols processing, and DL scheduling delay are included in the counter calculation. The DL scheduling delay is the dominant factor in the counter value.  In case of FDD Inter-band/Intra-band Carrier Aggregation with Two Flexi Zone Micro BTSs (LTE1858), the counter is applicable only to PCell traffic, that is, the SCell data is excluded.

Note: The PDCP, RLC, MAC protocols processing, and DL scheduling delay are included in the counter calculation. The DL scheduling delay is the dominant factor in the counter value.  In case of FDD Inter-band/Intra-band Carrier Aggregation with Two Flexi Zone Micro BTSs (LTE1858), the counter is applicable only to PCell traffic, that is, the SCell data is excluded.
4G|M8001C0.Updated: This counter is updated when the time starts at the reception of the PDCP SDU in the eNB and ends at the first transmission of a TB containing a segment of the SDU through the air interface. 4G|M8001C430.Description: This counter is part of the histogram "UE UL-Out-Of-Sync time" and provides the number of events when the measured Uplink-Out-Of-Sync time T of a UE was in the range 0 seconds < T <= 0.5 seconds.  The UE Uplink-Out-Of-Sync time T is measured by the eNB as the time between the UE state transition UL-In-Sync -> UL-Out-Of-Sync and the subsequent UE state transition UL-Out-Of-Sync -> UL-In-Sync. The counters which are part of the histogram "UE UL-Out-Of-Sync time" provide information regarding the distribution of the UL-Out-Of-Sync times of the UEs in the cell.

4G|M8005C206.Description: This measurement provides the minimum of the cell-wide RSSI value on PUCCH, which is calculated as: Total RSSI per cell per TTI for PUCCH over the configured PUCCH-bandwidth divided by the number of PRBs (of given whole cell non-blanked UL frequency bandwidth) which could be used by PUCCH in the cell.  This measurement does not include interference or noise. -130dBm is used if there is no UE in the cell.  Note regarding LTE2445: In case of combined supercells, the cell-wide PUCCH RSSI is the sum of the PUCCH RSSI measurements of all sub-cells.

Note regarding LTE3464: In case of UL MU-MIMO and massive MIMO combined together, the cell-wide RSSI for PUSCH is calculated as: total RSSI per cell per TTI for PUSCH from all layers over the complete channel bandwidth divided by the number of PRBs.

4G|M8005C281.Description: This measurement provides the minimum of the cell-wide SINR value on PUSCH, which is calculated as: total RSSI per cell per TTI for PUSCH over the complete channel bandwidth divided by the total interference power per cell per TTI for PUSCH over the complete channel bandwidth.  Note regarding LTE2445: In case of combined supercells, the cell-wide SINR for PUSCH is calculated using the sum of the PUSCH RSSI measurement values reported by all sub-cells, divided by the average interference power across all sub-cells.  Note regarding LTE3464: In case of UL MU-MIMO and massive MIMO combined together, the cell-wide SINR for PUSCH is calculated as:  total RSSI per cell per TTI for PUSCH from all layers over the complete channel bandwidth divided by the total of average I+N for each PRB per cell per TTI for PUSCH over the complete channel bandwidth. The average I+N for each PRB is the total of I+N from the available layers for each PRB divided by the number of available layer for each PRB.

The cell-wide SINR value is calculated as: total RSSI per cell per TTI for PUSCH over the complete channel bandwidth divided by the total interference power per cell per TTI for PUSCH over the complete channel bandwidth.  Note regarding LTE2445: In case of combined supercells, the cell-wide SINR for PUSCH is calculated using the sum of the PUSCH RSSI measurement values reported by all sub-cells, divided by the average interference power across all sub-cells.  Note regarding LTE3464: In case of UL MU-MIMO and massive MIMO combined together, the cell-wide SINR for PUSCH is calculated as:  total RSSI per cell per TTI for PUSCH from all layers over the complete channel bandwidth divided by the total of average I+N for each PRB per cell per TTI for PUSCH over the complete channel bandwidth. The average I+N for each PRB is the total of I+N from the available layers for each PRB divided by the number of available layer for each PRB.

4G|M8005C317.Description: This measurement provides the 50 percentile value of the uplink Interference Power over Thermal (IoT) Noise Power for the PUSCH Resource Block (RB) distribution bin 0. To increase the granularity, the counter is reported in 10* dB units.  To support the PUSCH RB distribution, there are 9 bins (bin0 to bin8). The PUSCH RBs would be evenly distributed (as much as possible) across the 9 bins with bin 0 and bin 8 having an equal number of PUSCH RBs.  Note regarding LTE2445: In case of combined supercells, both, interference power and thermal noise power are averaged over subcells before calculating IoT.  Note: In case of Fujitsu RRH it is possible to see this counter being pegged without any load on BTS. It is because Fujitsu RRH was designed to allow about 1dB for gain performance (variations) for Rx AMP. This design has no impact on system performance.

4G|M8006C89.Description: This counter denotes the number of EPC-initiated EPS Bearer Release requests for QCI1 due to normal release by UE. Each bearer of the "E-RAB to be Released List" IE is counted. In case of S1AP: PATH SWITCH REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE, the number of QCI1 E-RABs normally released in case that EPC has failed to perform the UP path switch for at least one (but not for all), and at least for one non-GBR E-RAB the UP path switch was successful, of the E-RABs included in the preceding S1AP: PATH SWITCH REQUEST is counted. The exception are the ERABs when the ERAB Release command was already sent previously for the same UE.

The exception are the ERABs when ERAB Release command was already sent previously for the same UE.

4G|M8006C244.Updated: This counter is updated following the transmission of an S1AP:INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE or an S1AP:INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message sent by the eNB to the MME.   S1AP:INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE: The counter is incremented by the number of bearers contained in the "E-RAB Failed to Setup List" IE with the RNL cause "Radio resources not available" (3GPP TS 36.413).   S1AP:INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE: The counter is incremented by the number of bearers contained in the "E-RAB to Be Setup List" IE of the preceding S1AP:INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST if the S1AP:INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE message is sent with the RNL cause "Radio resources not available" (3GPP TS 36.413).

4G|M8006C261.Description: This counter provides the number of E-RABs released due to the partial HO. Partial HO means that the HO for the admitted E-RABs was successfully completed, although not all the E-RABs were admitted by the HO target during HO preparation. The counter is incremented with the number of E-RABs not admitted by the HO target. The counter is maintained in the source cell, regardless of the bearer's QCI.
4G|M8006C261.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of E-RABs released due to the partial HO. Partial HO means that the HO for the admitted E-RABs was successfully completed, although not all the E-RABs were admitted by the HO target during HO preparation. The counter is incremented with the number of E-RABs not admitted by the HO target. The counter is maintained in the source cell, regardless of the bearer's QCI.
4G|M8006C261.Updated: Intra-eNB HO: The counter is updated upon reception of the eNB internal UE context release request message. The counter is incremented at the source cell with the number of bearers not admitted by the target eNB of the preceding HO preparation procedure. S1AP: E-RAB Release Indication to the MME informs about the E-RABs which have been released.  Inter-eNB HO via X2: Following the reception of the X2AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE message, the counter is incremented with the number of bearers not admitted by the target eNB of the preceding HO preparation procedure. The bearers, which are not admitted, are included in the "E-RABs Not Admitted List" IE of the X2AP:HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message that is received from the target eNB (3GPP TS 36.423).  Inter-eNB HO via S1 / Inter-system HO to UTRAN / SRVCC to UTRAN / Inter-system HO to SA NR: Following the reception of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message with the cause "RNL Successful Handover", the counter is incremented with the number of bearers, not admitted by the HO target of the preceding HO preparation procedure, only if the cause code of the S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message is NOT ‘successful-handover’. The bearers, which are not admitted, are included in the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND message that is received from MME (3GPP TS 36.413 / 38.413).
4G|M8006C261.Updated in previous release: Intra-eNB HO: The counter is updated upon reception of the eNB internal UE context release request message. The counter is incremented at the source cell with the number of bearers not admitted by the target eNB of the preceding HO preparation procedure. S1AP: E-RAB Release Indication to the MME informs about the E-RABs which have been released.  Inter-eNB HO via X2: Following the reception of the X2AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE message, the counter is incremented with the number of bearers not admitted by the target eNB of the preceding HO preparation procedure. The bearers, which are not admitted, are included in the "E-RABs Not Admitted List" IE of the X2AP:HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message that is received from the target eNB (3GPP TS 36.423).  Inter-eNB HO via S1 / Inter-system HO to UTRAN / SRVCC to UTRAN / Inter-system HO to SA NR: Following the reception of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message with the cause "RNL Successful Handover", the counter is incremented with the number of bearers, not admitted by the HO target of the preceding HO preparation procedure, only if the cause code of the S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message is NOT ‘successful-handover’. The bearers, which are not admitted, are included in the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND message that is received from MME (3GPP TS 36.413 / 38.413).

4G|M8006C291.Description: This counter provides the number of QCI2 E-RABs released due to the partial HO. Partial HO means that the HO for the admitted E-RABs was successfully completed, although not all E-RABs were admitted by the HO target during HO preparation. The counter is incremented with the number of QCI2 E-RABs not admitted by the HO target. The counter is maintained in the source cell.
4G|M8006C291.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of QCI2 E-RABs released due to the partial HO. Partial HO means that the HO for the admitted E-RABs was successfully completed, although not all E-RABs were admitted by the HO target during HO preparation. The counter is incremented with the number of QCI2 E-RABs not admitted by the HO target. The counter is maintained in the source cell.
4G|M8006C291.Updated: Intra-eNB HO: The counter is updated upon reception of eNB internal UE context release request message. The counter is incremented at the source cell with the number of QCI2 bearers not admitted by the target eNB of the preceding HO preparation procedure. S1AP: E-RAB Release Indication to the MME informs about the E-RABs which have been released.  Inter-eNB HO via X2: Following the reception of the X2AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE message, the counter is incremented with the number of QCI2 bearers not admitted by the target eNB of the preceding HO preparation procedure. The bearers, which are not admitted, are included in the "E-RABs Not Admitted List" IE of the X2AP:HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message that is received from the target eNB.  Inter-eNB HO via S1 / Inter-system HO to UTRAN / SRVCC to UTRAN / Inter-system HO to SA NR: Following the reception of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message with the cause "RNL Successful Handover", the counter is incremented with the number of QCI2 bearers not admitted by the HO target of the preceding HO preparation procedure, only if the cause code of the S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message is NOT �successful-handover�. The bearers, which are not admitted, are included in the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND message that is received from MME (3GPP TS 36.413 / 38.413).

4G|M8006C328.Description: This counter provides the number of released E-RABs of High Power UEs with abnormal release cause.  Note: A High Power UE is the one that has Power Class 1 or 2 capability.  Note: The E-RAB releases due to successful intra-LTE HO are also perceived as normal releases, but they are not counted in either normal or in abnormal release counter in order to be consistent with the existing E-RAB KPIs.  Note: An abnormal release leads to an unwanted release of an ERAB.
4G|M8006C328.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of released E-RABs of High Power UEs with abnormal release cause.  Note: A High Power UE is the one that has Power Class 1 or 2 capability.  Note: The E-RAB releases due to successful intra-LTE HO are also perceived as normal releases, but they are not counted in either normal or in abnormal release counter in order to be consistent with the existing E-RAB KPIs.  Note: An abnormal release leads to an unwanted release of an ERAB.
4G|M8006C328.Updated: This counter is updated upon abnormal release of an ERAB by the eNB for Power Class 1 or 2 UEs.  The following are considered to be abnormal releases: Partial handover through S1:  1. not admitted bearers from the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message are counted only in case when the cause code from the given message is NOT �successful-handover�, and  2. after S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND reception the S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message must be received with RNL cause "Successful Handover".  Partial handover through X2 - not admitted bearers from the "E-RABs Not Admitted List" of the X2AP: HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message when X2AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE message is received.  eNB initiated E-RAB release - S1AP: E-RAB RELEASE INDICATION is sent.  eNB-initiated UE context release due to a reason other than user inactivity or UE redirect - S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with the RNL cause other than "User Inactivity", "Inter-RAT redirection", "Redirection towards 1xRTT", "CS Fallback Triggered", "UE Not Available For PS Service", or "E-UTRAN Generated Reason" is sent (Remark: S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with "E-UTRAN Generated Reason" RNL cause can be also sent due to a procedure other than UE redirect. Such should be considered an abnormal case).  MME-initiated E-RAB or UE context release due to a reason other than normal call end or detach procedure - S1AP: E-RAB RELEASE COMMAND or S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND with NAS cause other than "Normal release" or "Detach" is received.  This counter is not incremented in case when the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND is received as a response to a previously sent S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST.  Failed path switch - bearers for which path switch failed from the "E-RAB To Be Released List" of the received S1AP: PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLDEGE message for any cause except "NAS: Normal Release".  S1 Setup, Reset or Link failure - RRC: RRC CONNECTION RELEASE is sent due to S1 Setup, Reset or Link Failure procedures. 4G|M8006C334.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of setup attempts from MME for additional E-RABs of QCI1, but excludes any retries from the MME for the same UE while eNB handling for the original MME request was still on-going.
4G|M8006C334.Updated: This counter is updated with the number of QCI1 bearers contained in the "E-RAB to Be Setup List" of an S1AP:E-RAB SETUP REQUEST when the eNB receives this message from the MME, but excludes any MME retries for the same UE.  The MME retry attempts may occur if an RRC Reconfiguration procedure for the UE was on-going at the eNB when the original ERAB SETUP REQUEST containing QCI1 was received and then rejected (due to an interaction with the on-going RRC procedure).  The MME retry will be rejected by S1AP: E-RAB SETUP RESPONSE with cause RNL (X2 Handover triggered), RNL (S1 Intra-System Handover triggered), RNL (S1 Inter-System Handover triggered), or other cause code, depending on the scenario, or rejected internally within the eNB without sending any S1AP: E-RAB SETUP RESPONSE, which is relevant for scenario when MME retry, and its final outcome is received after the eNB sent UE Context Release Request to MME.   In Inter-eNB HO cases including Inter-eNB "RLF-triggered HO", cause code "X2 Handover triggered" or "S1 Intra-System Handover triggered" in ERAB SETUP RESPONSE means that the MME will retry with the target or new-serving eNB if the Inter-eNB HO or RLF-triggered HO is successful.  Note: Inter-eNB RLF-triggered HO can occur not only after reception of ERAB Setup Request(QCI1) while Inter-eNB X2/S1 HO is on-going or while IRAT is on-going, but also while Intra-Cell/Intra-eNB HO is on-going or while non-HO procedure such as CA Config/Deconfig/Reconfig is on-going.  In the Intra-Cell/Intra-eNB HO and non-HO procedure cases, the eNB buffers the original ERAB SETUP REQUEST message and de-queues the message when the RLF Indication arrives from a neighbor eNB; the eNB shall set cause code "X2 HO Triggered" in ERAB SETUP RESPONSE as part of RLF-triggered HO procedure.

4G|M8007C14.Description: This measurement provides the mean E-RAB setup time (3GPP TS 32.425, 36.413, 23.203).
4G|M8007C14.Description in previous release: This measurement provides the mean E-RAB setup time (3GPP TS 32.425, 36.413, 23.203).
4G|M8007C14.Updated: This measurement is obtained by accumulating the time intervals for every successfully established E-RAB between the reception of an E-RAB SETUP REQUEST or INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message and the transmission of the corresponding E-RAB SETUP RESPONSE or INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message by the eNB over the granularity period. The end value of this time will then be divided by the number of successfully established E-RABs in the granularity period to give the arithmetic mean. The accumulator is reinitialized at the beginning of each granularity period. Note: The measurement is initialized with "0" at the beginning of each granularity period. A measurement result "0" at the end of the granularity period (for example, 15 minutes) means that no E-RAB setup occurred in the cell during the whole granularity period and that the measurement does not contain a valid measurement result.

4G|M8008C17.Description: This measurement provides the mean RRC connection setup time (3GPP TS 32.425, 36.331).
4G|M8008C17.Description in previous release: This measurement provides the mean RRC connection setup time (3GPP TS 32.425, 36.331).
4G|M8008C17.Updated: This measurement is obtained by accumulating the time intervals for every successful RRC connection establishment between the reception of an RRCConnectionRequest and the corresponding RRCConnectionSetupComplete message by the eNB over the granularity period. The end value of this time will then be divided by the number of successful RRC connections observed in the granularity period to give the arithmetic mean. The accumulator is reinitialized at the beginning of each granularity period. Note: The measurement is initialized with "0" at the beginning of each granularity period. A measurement result "0" at the end of the granularity period (for example, 15 minutes) means that no RRC connection setup occurred in the cell during the whole granularity period and that the measurement does not contain a valid measurement result.

4G|M8008C32.Description: This counter provides the total number of SCG split bearers with NR PDCP for DRB establishment attempts during the execution phase of the SgNB Addition procedure. This is due to the fact that attempt would be pegged on the source MeNB while succeeding on the target MeNB.

4G|M8008C40.Description: This counter provides the Number of RRC Connection Re-establishment attempts for QCI1.   Note: This counter is only pegged if the Context Fetch procedure is successful.
4G|M8008C40.Description in previous release: This counter provides the Number of RRC Connection Re-establishment attempts for QCI1.   Note: This counter is only pegged if the Context Fetch procedure is successful.
4G|M8008C40.Updated: This counter is updated when an RRCConnectionReestablishmentRequest message is received by the eNB and the presence of QCI1 ERAB is determined from the UE Context.  Note 1. If the Reestablishment is to the Prepared (source or target) Cell, the UE Context is known.  Note 2. If the Reestablishment is to the Unprepared Cell, the UE Context needs to be fetched with an RLF Triggered Handover (reception of X2AP: Handover Request message with QCI1 bearer). In case of an Intra eNB RLF handover the context is fetched with an internal message.
4G|M8008C40.Updated in previous release: This counter is updated when an RRCConnectionReestablishmentRequest message is received by the eNB and the presence of QCI1 ERAB is determined from the UE Context.  Note 1. If the Reestablishment is to the Prepared (source or target) Cell, the UE Context is known.  Note 2. If the Reestablishment is to the Unprepared Cell, the UE Context needs to be fetched with an RLF Triggered Handover (reception of X2AP: Handover Request message with QCI1 bearer). In case of an Intra eNB RLF handover the context is fetched with an internal message.

4G|M8008C47.Network Element Name in previous release: Mean RRC connection setup time with cause 'HPA'

4G|M8008C47.Description: This counter provides the mean RRC connection setup time with cause 'HPA".
4G|M8008C47.Description in previous release: This counter provides the mean RRC connection setup time with cause 'HPA".
4G|M8008C47.Updated: This counter is updated by accumulating the time intervals for every successful RRC connection establishment with cause 'HPA' between the reception of an RRCConnectionRequest and the corresponding RRCConnectionSetupComplete message by the eNB over the granularity period. The end value of this time will then be divided by the number of successful RRC connections observed in the granularity period to give the arithmetic mean. The accumulator is reinitialized at the beginning of each granularity period. Note: The counter is initialized with "0" at the beginning of each granularity period. A counter result "0" at the end of the granularity period (for example, 15 minutes) means that no RRC connection setup occurred in the cell during the whole granularity period and that the counter does not contain a valid counter result.

4G|M8010C62.Description: This counter provides the number of dedicated PDCCH resource allocations (eNB -> UE) for PDSCH transmissions with HARQ reporting in case that the eNB was not able to detect the HARQ response (ACK/NACK) from the UE; that is this counter provides the number of dedicated PDCCH resource allocations by which the eNB informs a dedicated UE on the PDCCH about the allocated PDSCH resources which are used for PDSCH transmissions with HARQ reporting in case that the eNB was not able to detect the HARQ response (ACK/NACK) from the UE. This counter is only updated when the eNB was not able to detect the HARQ response (ACK/NACK) from the UE. Therefore, either a transmission error for the downlink PDCCH resource allocation (eNB -> UE) or a transmission error for the uplink HARQ response (UE -> eNB) has occurred.

4G|M8010C94.Product Type: AirScale SBTS,ASM FDD,ASM TDD,Flexi SBTS,FSM-r3 FDD,FSM-r3 TDD
4G|M8010C94.Product Type in previous release: AirScale SBTS,ASM FDD,ASM TDD,Flexi SBTS,FSM-r3 FDD,FSM-r3 TDD
4G|M8010C94.Description: The percentage of suppressed OFDM symbols with micro DTX to all transmitted symbols in the FS module.  The percentage is obtained from the average value of all samples across all MIMO paths.  For each sample with a duration of 120 ms, the percentage of suppressed symbols to all transmitted symbols is calculated.  Note1: Feature LTE3036 extends the functionality of the LTE1891 with new patterns that act as guidelines that in some cases doesn’t mute the symbols even if the pattern requires the opposite.  Note2: There are certain cases in which a fallback is needed from the full LTE3036 operation to the LTE1891. In this case, the counter shall combine the results of both.  Note3: In case Traffic Concentration / active muting pattern (LTE1891 or LTE3036) is done, the counter shows cell view (MAC-PS), which may differ with RF module final decision, but still is able to catch possible energy-saving occasions. In case TC / active muting pattern is not done, or when empty subframes happen to fall outside muted TTIs in a pattern, the counter is updated with zero values.

4G|M8011C69.Description: This counter indicates the occurrence that the cell is in the active Load Balancing state for inter-frequency load balancing. When the cell is in the active Load Balancing state, the Load Balancing algorithm tries to reduce the serving cell load by shifting the cell traffic to neighbor cells (Load Balancing handover). The maximum value of this counter depends on the length of the measurement period. If the measurement period is 15 minutes (that is, 900 sec), the maximum value of this counter is 900 sec/1 sec = 900 (every 1 second, the eNB checks whether the cell is in the active Load Balancing state).

4G|M8011C81.Product Type in previous release: AirScale SBTS,ASM FDD,ASM TDD,Flexi SBTS,FSM-r3 FDD,FSM-r3 TDD
4G|M8011C81.Description: This counter is a part of the histogram "Cell DL Composite Available Capacity (DL CAC)" and provides the number of events when the measured downlink CAC of the cell was zero (DL CAC = 0). Load balancing is activated to shift traffic from the high-loaded LTE serving cell to the lower-loaded LTE neighbor cell by favoring handovers from the serving cell to the neighbor cell (by applying neighbor-cell-related handover thresholds which favor handovers to the neighbor cell). The DL CAC of the cell is measured by the eNB internally and is used by the eNB in the context of cell load measurements for load balancing between cells (3GPP TS 36.423). A DL CAC value "0" indicates no available capacity, and value "100" indicates maximum available capacity in the cell (see 3GPP TS 36.423).

4G|M8011C90.Description: This counter is a part of the histogram "Cell DL Available Capacity for PDCCH" and provides the number of events when the measured PDCCH AC of the cell was zero (PDCCH AC = 0). Load balancing is activated to shift traffic from the high-loaded LTE serving cell to the lower-loaded LTE neighbor cell by favoring handovers from the serving cell to the neighbor cell (by applying neighbor-cell-related handover thresholds that favor handovers to the neighbor cell). The PDCCH AC of the cell is measured by the eNB internally and is used by the eNB in the context of cell load measurements for load balancing between cells (3GPP TS 36.423). A PDCCH AC value of "0" indicates no available capacity, and a value of "100" indicates maximum available capacity in the cell (see 3GPP TS 36.423).

4G|M8011C106.Counter Description: This counter is a part of the histogram "Cell DL Available Capacity (DL AC) for non-GBR bearers" and provides the number of events when the measured downlink AC for non-GBR bearers of the cell was in the range 60 < DL non-GBR AC <= 80. Load balancing is activated to shift traffic from the high-loaded LTE serving cell to the lower-loaded LTE neighbor cell by favoring handovers from the serving cell to the neighbor cell (by applying neighbor-cell-related handover thresholds that favor handovers to the neighbor cell). The DL non-GBR AC of the cell is measured by the eNB internally and is used by the eNB in the context of cell load measurements for load balancing between cells (3GPP TS 36.423). A DL non-GBR AC value of "0" indicates no available capacity, and a value of "100" indicates maximum available capacity in the cell (see 3GPP TS 36.423).

4G|M8011C162.Network Element Name: High cell load indicator for load balancing to UTRAN
4G|M8011C162.Network Element Name in previous release: High cell load indicator for load balancing to UTRAN
4G|M8011C162.Description: This counter indicates the occurrence that the cell is in the active load balancing state for load balancing to UTRAN. When the cell is in the active load balancing state, the load balancing algorithm tries to reduce the LTE serving cell load by shifting the cell traffic to UTRAN neighbor cells (load balancing handover).  The maximum value of this counter depends on the length of the measurement period. If the measurement period is 15 minutes (that is 900 s), the maximum value of this counter is 900 s/1 s+F3 = 900 (every 1 second, the eNB checks whether the cell is in the active load balancing state for load balancing to UTRAN).

4G|M8011C182.Network Element Name: UL PRB utilization in center PUSCH region on A-MPR-enabled cell per TTI mean
4G|M8011C182.Network Element Name in previous release: UL PRB utilization in center PUSCH region on A-MPR-enabled cell per TTI mean
4G|M8011C182.Description: This counter provides the mean value of the UL Physical Resource Block (PRB) utilization per TTI in the center PUSCH region on an A-MPR-enabled cell. The reported value is 10 times higher than the actual value (for example 5.4 is stored as 54).  Note1: The center region consists of all of the PRBs surrounded by the adjacent PUCCH channels. Note2: In case of interworking with feature LTE4611, the counter does not include the allocations across lower/center/upper PUSCH regions of the single connected UE that is handled by LTE4611 (i.e., counter doesn't include any allocations when UE can use up to 100 PRBs, and in case of PRACH TTI up to a maximum of 64 PRBs, which overlaps with any 2 or 3 PUSCH regions, irrespective of finally allocated PRBs for UE based on available data and PHR). Note3. This counter is not supported with band19_NS08 because there are no lower/center/upper PUSCH regions with feature CB007828.

4G|M8011C216.Network Element Name: Number of successful DRS transmissions on LTE-U/LAA cell
4G|M8011C216.Network Element Name in previous release: Number of successful DRS transmissions on LTE-U/LAA cell
4G|M8011C216.Description: This counter provides the total number of successful DRS-only transmissions on the LTE-U/LAA cell. Discovery Reference Signals (DRS) should be transmitted within DMTC (DRS Measurement Timing Configuration) window (6 consecutive sub-frames), or if this window overlaps with a PDSCH transmission burst during sub-frame #0 or #5 during the PDSCH (Physical Downlink Shared Channel) transmission burst. This counter tracks the number of successful DRS-only transmissions, but it does not include successful DRS+PDSCH transmissions.

This counter tracks the number of successful DRS-only transmissions, but it does not include successful DRS+PDSCH transmissions.
4G|M8011C216.Updated: This counter is updated with an eNB-internal trigger. The eNB increments the counter in case the DRS-only transmission was successful.

4G|M8011C220.Description: This counter provides the total number of failed data transmit bursts on the LTE-U/LAA cell. A failed data transmit burst is not automatically retried and new LTE-U/LAA data transmissions require a new transmit burst request.

4G|M8011C248.Network Element Name: Number of times when IDC hardware sharing problem with LAA is reported
4G|M8011C248.Network Element Name in previous release: Number of times when IDC hardware sharing problem with LAA is reported
4G|M8011C248.Description: This counter shows the total number of times when a UE, with configured LAA SCells, has begun experiencing IDC hardware sharing problem with LAA.
4G|M8011C248.Description in previous release: This counter shows the total number of times when a UE, with configured LAA SCells, has begun experiencing IDC hardware sharing problem with LAA.
4G|M8011C248.Updated: This counter is incremented each time when an eNB receives indication that the UE is experiencing IDC hardware sharing problem with LAA. The indication is within hardwareSharingProblem-r13 IE, which is included in InDeviceCoexIndication-r11 message that is sent from a UE to the eNB (according to 3GPP TS 36.331).  Note: It is counted only once, when the message is first received from UE or in AS-Context. Subsequent reports on the same PCell in the same RRC connection, during which the issue is already active, shall not increment this counter.
4G|M8011C248.Updated in previous release: This counter is incremented each time when an eNB receives indication that the UE is experiencing IDC hardware sharing problem with LAA. The indication is within hardwareSharingProblem-r13 IE, which is included in InDeviceCoexIndication-r11 message that is sent from a UE to the eNB (according to 3GPP TS 36.331).  Note: It is counted only once, when the message is first received from UE or in AS-Context. Note 1: The throughput calculation is based on the data volume send in the PDCP SDUs. Therefore, any data transmitted through SCell in CA scenario is counted at the PCell.  Note 2: The throughput from Cat-M and NB IoT UEs is excluded.  Note 3: The throughput for intra-site inter-eNB CA UEs includes PDCP SDU data sent from PCell and SCell Physical.  Note 4: The throughput for inter-site inter-eNB CA UEs includes PDCP SDU data sent to PCell Physical and PDCP SDU data sent to SCell scheduling over X2.

4G|M8012C91.Product Type in previous release: AirScale SBTS,ASM FDD,ASM TDD,Flexi SBTS,FSM-r3 FDD,FSM-r3 TDD
4G|M8012C91.Description: This counter provides the aggregated IP throughput volume on QCI 1 bearers in uplink as experienced by the UE.  Note: The throughput measurement according to 3GPP TS 36.314 is suitable for services with packet sizes or data bursts that are large enough to require transmissions to be split across several consecutive TTIs. However, regarding the QCI1 service, usually, majority of the transmission is done through one TTI burst only, and therefore not counted. That is why this counter should not be used for evaluation of QCI1 service because it usually reflects minority of the QCI1 traffic. An alternative for QCI1 throughput evaluation is to use QCI1 PDCP SDU active cell throughput PDCP_DATA_RATE_MEAN_UL_QCI_1 (M8012C116) instead.

However, regarding the QCI1 service, usually, majority of the transmission is done through one TTI burst only, and therefore not counted. That is why this counter should not be used for evaluation of QCI1 service because it usually reflects minority of the QCI1 traffic. An alternative for QCI1 throughput evaluation is to use QCI1 PDCP SDU active cell throughput PDCP_DATA_RATE_MEAN_UL_QCI_1 (M8012C116) instead.
4G|M8012C91.Updated: This counter is updated when the volume of a data burst excluding the data transmitted in the TTI when the buffer is emptied. A sample for ThpVolUl is the data volume counted on PDCP SDU level in bits received in UL for one E-RAB during a sample of ThpTimeUl. (It must exclude the volume of the last piece of data emptying the buffer).

4G|M8012C117.Description: This counter provides the aggregated IP throughput volume on QCI 1 bearers in downlink as experienced by the UE.  Note: The throughput measurement according to 3GPP TS 36.314 is suitable for services with packet sizes or data bursts that are large enough to require transmissions to be split across several consecutive TTIs. However, regarding the QCI1 service, usually majority of the transmission is done through one TTI burst only, and therefore not counted. That is why this counter should not be used for evaluation of QCI1 service because it usually reflects minority of the QCI1 traffic. An alternative for QCI1 throughput evaluation, is to use QCI1 PDCP SDU active cell throughput PDCP_DATA_RATE_MEAN_DL_QCI_1 (M8012C143) instead.

4G|M8012C156.Description: This measurement provides the IP throughput time on QCI 1 bearers in uplink. It excludes TTIs in that there was data in the buffer but the UE was not scheduled.  Note: The throughput measurement according to 3GPP TS 36.314 is suitable for services with packet sizes or data bursts that are large enough to require transmissions to be split across several consecutive TTIs. However, regarding the QCI1 service, the transmission is usually done through only one TTI bursts. That is why this counter does not need to represent all QCI1 UEs, and thus, the overall situation in the observed cell is not monitored.

4G|M8012C179.Network Element Name in previous release: Average achievable MAC PDU Throughput in Downlink per Cell
4G|M8012C179.Description: This counter provides the average achievable MAC PDU Cell Throughput in Downlink. Achievable is when all of the available PDSCH bandwidth in the carrier is used.  In the sampling interval (1s), the achievable downlink throughput is calculated as the MAC PDU DL data bits are divided by the PRB utilization factor that is defined as: [(number of DL PRBs used to carry the data) / (available DL PRBs for PDSCH transmission)]. The HARQ retransmission and overhead are excluded from the MAC PDU DL data bits. Meanwhile, PRB consumption include both the new and the retransmitted HARQ PRBs. The average is calculated at the end of measurement period.   Note: Only the samples for which the PRB Utilization is higher than the threshold value configured with parameter cfgPRBUtilThreshold are considered.  Note: The data volume transmitted over the PCell and all of the SCells for the CA UEs is incremented to the physical cell where the data was transferred.

The HARQ retransmission and overhead are excluded from the MAC PDU UL data bits. Meanwhile, PRB consumptions include both the new and the retransmitted HARQ PRBs.   Note: Only the samples for which the PRB Utilization is higher than the configured threshold value with parameter cfgPRBUtilThreshold are considered.  Note: The data volume transmitted over the PCell and all of the SCells for the CA UEs and their number is incremented to the physical cell where the data was transferred.

4G|M8012C218.Description: This counter provides the sum of initial burst scheduling applicability and scheduling delay for UEs with CA Activity in Downlink for non-GBR traffic (QCIs 6-9). The delay time is calculated starting from the time the data is received to an empty PDCP buffer and ending at the time for the first scheduling of the data for the UE. This includes L2(RLC, MAC) and L1 processing time from the scheduling to actual transmission in a TTI.  Note1: Bursts that arrive before previous burst is completed are excluded. Note3: UEs with CA activity is considered when at least 1 SCell is active when the UE is taken into scheduling candidate set.  Note4: Only non-GBR ERABs shall be considered (QCI6, QCI7, QCI8, and QCI9).   Note5: This counter is incremented to the PCell only.

Note for inter-site Carrier Aggregation: In case that the last part of data burst (except the last TTI emptying the buffer) is transmitted over SCell, the time interval that this part of the data burst spends in the RLC buffer of the SCell is estimated from the point in time when the corresponding RLC PDU was sent from PCell to SCell to the point in time when the corresponding RLC PDU is scheduled for transmission in the SCell.  Note: Please check the LTE5077 feature description for detailed information on counter pegging mechanism.

All data bytes (including headers) sent (excluding retransmissions) by the cell for all CA-configured users with their SCell being the EutranCell where this counter is pegged.
4G|M8012C223.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of bytes sent over the MAC interface in the downlink direction related to Carrier-Aggregation-configured (CA-configured)  UE traffic in the SCell. The measurement is made at PDU level and is made only for a UE that is configured and activated with CA. It excludes MAC retransmissions, but TRB and SRB are considered.  All data bytes (including headers) sent (excluding retransmissions) by the cell for all CA-configured users with their SCell being the EutranCell where this counter is pegged.
4G|M8012C223.Updated: This counter is triggered when a CA-activated UE in SCell transmits a MAC PDU at MAC layer for any TRB or SRB excluding the MAC retransmissions.  NOTE: A fresh transmission is considered when fresh packets are sent on any codewords.  In addition, if multiple codewords are involved and at least one codeword is used to transmit fresh packets while other codewords are carrying retransmitted packets, the fresh packets will be counted. The number of bytes of the MAC PDU is then added to the matching screening.

4G|M8012C259.Description: This counter provides the IP throughput time on QCI65 bearers in uplink. It excludes TTIs in which there was data in the buffer but the UE was not scheduled.  Note: The throughput measurement according to 3GPP TS 36.314 is suitable for services with packet sizes or data bursts that are large enough to require transmissions to be split across several consecutive TTIs. However, regarding the QCI65 service, the transmission is usually done through only one TTI burst. 4G|M8012C267.Updated: This counter is triggered according to 3GPP TS 36.314 with the fraction of TTIs of single TTI bursts calculated as follows:  ThpTimeDl=TTI*(TBVol-PaddingVol)/TBVol  Where:   1. TTI is the duration of the TTI. 2. TBVol is the Volume of the TB related to one TTI burst and represents UE achievable TB size. 3. PaddingVol is the Volume of padding bits added into Transport Block related to one TTI burst. TBVol-PaddingVol is an MAC PDU volume to which bearer specific PDCP SDU volume of the single TTI burst is mapped in MAC layer excluding padding bits.   The counting is done only for non-CA UEs, that is, UEs with no activated SCell. It means the counter data is measured in each TTI for all standard non-GBR (QCI5-9) E-RABs for which non-CA UE has a data burst ongoing. A sample of ThpTimeDl for each time the DL buffer for one E-RAB is emptied.  Note: The time duration for HARQ retransmissions is included. Therefore, the resulting throughput is lower with degraded radio conditions.

4G|M8012C294.Updated: The volume of a data burst excluding the data transmitted in the TTI when the buffer is emptied. A sample for ThpVolDl is the data volume, counted on the PDCP SDU level, in bits transmitted in DL for one E-RAB during a sample of ThpTimeDl. It must exclude the volume of the last piece of data emptying the buffer. 4G|M8012C304.Description: This counter provides the IP throughput data volume on nonGBR E-RABs in downlink (transferred by the PDCP layer) for UEs without activated CA, that is UEs with no SCell activated.  Note: nonGBR here means ERABs with QCI5, QCI6, QCI7,QCI8 and QCI9.   Note: Legacy method means the calculation method used before LTE5625 feature.  Note: This counter is supported for AirScale only.
4G|M8012C304.Description in previous release: This counter provides the IP throughput data volume on nonGBR E-RABs in downlink (transferred by the PDCP layer) for UEs without activated CA, that is UEs with no SCell activated. 4G|M8012C304.Updated: This counter is triggered according to 3GPP TS 36.314 except that the counting is done only for non-CA UEs, that is UEs with no activated SCell. It means sample for ThpVolDl is the data volume, counted on the PDCP SDU level, in bits successfully transmitted (acknowledged by the UE) in DL for all E-RAB during a sample of ThpTimeDl excluding the volume of the last piece of data emptying the buffer. In addition, it considers counting part of the PDCP SDU when SCell(s) is not active for the whole PDCP SDU duration.

4G|M8013C3.Description: This counter provides the number of Initial Context Setup Request procedure failures due to the following RRC Re-establishment scenarios:  1. There is a reception of RrcConnectionReestablishmentRequest or intra-eNB RLF Indication after the reception of RRCSecurityModeComplete and before the reception of RRCConnectionReconfigurationComplete.  2. There is a reception of RLF Indication from a neighbor eNB while the RRC Reconfig procedure was on-going (a neighbor eNB cell had received RRC Reestablishment Request that triggered the transmission of RLF Indication back to this eNB, that is, detection of RLF by the neighbor eNB).  3. There is a reception of UE Context Release Command with cause "Radio Connection with UE Lost" from the MME while the RRC Reconfiguration procedure was on-going (detection of RLF by MME in the form of Double S1).  4. There is a reception of UE Context Release Command with a cause other than "Radio Conn with UE Lost", "Normal Release", "Detach", "CS Fallback Triggered", or "Successful Handover" from the MME while the RRC Reconfiguration procedure was on-going.  Note: This counter shall be mutually exclusive with the counter UE_CTX_SETUP_FAIL_MAX_RLC_RTR for the same Failure of UE Context.

Note: This counter shall be mutually exclusive with the counter UE_CTX_SETUP_FAIL_MAX_RLC_RTR for the same Failure of UE Context.

4G|M8013C76.Description: This counter shows the number of released UE Contexts initiated by the eNB with the radio network layer cause "Inter-RAT redirection" due to coverage reasons.  Note 1: Redirects due to coverage reasons come from LTE423 RRC connection release with redirect to NR, WCDMA, GSM, eHRPD, CDMA/1xRTT, and LTE1073 Measurement-based Redirect to UTRAN, excluding cases when the trigger of a redirect is LTE736 CS Fallback to UTRAN.  Note 2: S1AP: UE Context Release Request with cause "Inter-RAT redirection" in case of eNACC to GSM and supervision timer TeNACCoverall expires (error handling) are excluded. Redirect events towards Home eNodeB are excluded.  Note 3: Measurement-based redirections to GERAN are currently not supported.

4G|M8013C104.Updated: This counter is incremented by one after the transmission of an S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message from the eNB to the MME when inter-RAT redirection is triggered. This covers any redirection to NR, HRPD, UTRAN FDD, UTRAN TDD, and GERAN with any trigger including CS fallback.  The cause code 'Redirection towards 1xRTT' shall be used for redirection to 1xCSFB due to the following reasons:  a. RRC Connection release without redirectedCarrierInfo IE in the message followed by an S1 release b. due to Measurement-based Rel8 redirection to 1xRTT c. due to Blind Rel8 redirection to 1xRTT  Both Forced Rel-8 1xCSFB redirection and enhanced 1xCSFB are excluded (see counters UE_CTX_REL_ENB_RL8_CSFB_RD and UE_CTX_REL_ENB_ECSFB_SUCC).  The following cause codes shall be used in other cases: - "inter-RAT Redirection" (in case of IRAT redirection to NR/UTRAN/GERAN); - "CS Fallback triggered" (in case of CSFB to UTRAN, or in case of CSFB to GERAN when the UE is DTM capable); - "UE Not Available for PS Service" (in case of CSFB to GERAN when the UE and/or GERAN cell has no DTM capability).  Mobility to the Home eNB or Hybrid eNB using UE Context Releases for redirection due to "Inter-RAT Redirection" is excluded from this counter.

4G|M8013C113.Updated: "This counter is incremented by one upon the transmission of an S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message sent by the eNB to the MME with the release cause ""RNL Radio Connection With UE Lost"", which is triggered by RRC Guard timer expiry (with the exception of THOOverall timer expiration).  The trigger "expiration of THOOverall" is excluded because in case of a failed intra eNB HO, the counter UE_CTX_REL_ENB_IN_LTE_HO_TO is updated (3GPP TS 36.413).  RRC connection reconfiguration guard timer RRCGuardTimerRadioBearerManagement may timeout in the following non-HO RRC Reconfiguration scenarios: Initial Context Setup, including SMC and UE Cap Enquiry procedure;  ERAB Modify/Setup/Release;  Various measurement reconfigurations;  CA configuration (SCell addition, Release, Reselect) and CA de-config; Eicic Sib1 Update using dedicated RRC Reconfiguration (Introduced by LTE2208).

The trigger "expiration of THOOverall" is excluded because in case of a failed intra eNB HO, the counter UE_CTX_REL_ENB_IN_LTE_HO_TO is updated (3GPP TS 36.413).  RRC connection reconfiguration guard timer RRCGuardTimerRadioBearerManagement may timeout in the following non-HO RRC Reconfiguration scenarios: Initial Context Setup, including SMC and UE Cap Enquiry procedure;  ERAB Modify/Setup/Release;  Various measurement reconfigurations;  CA configuration (SCell addition, Release, Reselect) and CA de-config; Eicic Sib1 Update using dedicated RRC Reconfiguration (Introduced by LTE2208).

4G|M8015C16.Description: This counter provides the number of Late Handovers per neighbor cell relationship. A Late Handover is a sequence of a missed HO attempt (instead of HO, RLF on the UE side and optionally recoverable RLF on the eNB side) in one cell followed by an RRC connection re-establishment request in another cell.   In case of an intra cell handover, this counter shall not be updated. Reason: This MRO-related counter, which is used by the MRO algorithm (LTE533: Mobility Robustness Optimization), is an inter cell handover related counter (that is the handover target cell is different from the handover source cell) which shall not be influenced by intra cell handovers (that is handover target cell is equal to handover source cell).   Note: Handovers for UEs with modified CIO settings are excluded from this counter.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case the LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.
4G|M8015C16.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of Late Handovers per neighbor cell relationship. A Late Handover is a sequence of a missed HO attempt (instead of HO, RLF on the UE side and optionally recoverable RLF on the eNB side) in one cell followed by an RRC connection re-establishment request in another cell.   In case of an intra cell handover, this counter shall not be updated. Reason: This MRO-related counter, which is used by the MRO algorithm (LTE533: Mobility Robustness Optimization), is an inter cell handover related counter (that is the handover target cell is different from the handover source cell) which shall not be influenced by intra cell handovers (that is handover target cell is equal to handover source cell).   Note: Handovers for UEs with modified CIO settings are excluded from this counter.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case the LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.
4G|M8015C16.Updated: Reception of X2AP:RLF INDICATION message satisfying the following conditions: - C-RNTI corresponds to an available UE context - shortMAC-I is included - shortMAC-I matches the local security calculation (successful authentication) - Tstore_UE_cntxt timer associated with the corresponding authenticated shortMAC-I is not running Source cell: A cell receiving the X2AP:RLF INDICATION message is received (source cell of missed HO attempt and optional recoverable RLF on eNB side) Target cell:  A cell sending X2AP:RLF INDICATION message (cell receiving the re-establishment request after missed HO attempt) The counter is incremented at the source cell per neighbor cell (target cell) Notes: The case of re-establishment causes that "ReconfigFailure" is excluded from counting. The case of re-establishment causes that "HOfailure" is excluded from counting when the re-establishment target cell is prepared for the incoming HO, as this means the HO has been attempted, not missed. In case of re-establishment request to cell prepared for the incoming HO, the case of received PCI being different from the source cell PCI of the prepared HO is excluded from counting. In the source cell of missed HO attempt, an HO preparation for the considered UE context might be ongoing. The target cell of such HO preparation can be different from the cell receiving the re-establishment request.  In case of an intra cell handover the counter shall not be updated.
4G|M8015C16.Updated in previous release: Reception of X2AP:RLF INDICATION message satisfying the following conditions: - C-RNTI corresponds to an available UE context - shortMAC-I is included - shortMAC-I matches the local security calculation (successful authentication) - Tstore_UE_cntxt timer associated with the corresponding authenticated shortMAC-I is not running Source cell: A cell receiving the X2AP:RLF INDICATION message is received (source cell of missed HO attempt and optional recoverable RLF on eNB side) Target cell:  A cell sending X2AP:RLF INDICATION message (cell receiving the re-establishment request after missed HO attempt) The counter is incremented at the source cell per neighbor cell (target cell) Notes: The case of re-establishment causes that "ReconfigFailure" is excluded from counting. The case of re-establishment causes that "HOfailure" is excluded from counting when the re-establishment target cell is prepared for the incoming HO, as this means the HO has been attempted, not missed. In case of re-establishment request to cell prepared for the incoming HO, the case of received PCI being different from the source cell PCI of the prepared HO is excluded from counting. In the source cell of missed HO attempt, an HO preparation for the considered UE context might be ongoing. The target cell of such HO preparation can be different from the cell receiving the re-establishment request.  In case of an intra cell handover the counter shall not be updated.

4G|M8015C16.Counter Description: This counter provides the number of Late Handovers per neighbor cell relationship. A Late Handover is a sequence of a missed HO attempt (instead of HO, RLF on the UE side and optionally recoverable RLF on the eNB side) in one cell followed by an RRC connection re-establishment request in another cell.   In case of an intra cell handover, this counter shall not be updated. Reason: This MRO-related counter, which is used by the MRO algorithm (LTE533: Mobility Robustness Optimization), is an inter cell handover related counter (that is the handover target cell is different from the handover source cell) which shall not be influenced by intra cell handovers (that is handover target cell is equal to handover source cell).   Note: Handovers for UEs with modified CIO settings are excluded from this counter.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case the LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

4G|M8015C20.Description: This measurement provides the number of Ping Pong handovers per neighbor cell relationship.  A Ping Pong handover is a sequence of handovers whereby a UE is handed over from an LTE cell A to an LTE neighbor cell B and finally returns to the same cell A within a short time period (defined by the parameter tPingPong).  This measurement consists of neighbor cell-related handover counters; that is, for each handover neighbor cell relationship between cell A and its neighbor cells (for example, cell B), a separate Ping Pong handover counter is provided.  Remark: If the first handover event between cell A and a neighbor cell B leads to a Ping Pong handover then this counter will not be incremented for this first Ping Pong handover because this first handover event triggers the creation of the counter which can then be used for successive handover events. That is, the counter is incremented for successive handover events which occur after the first handover event.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case the LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

4G|M8021C7.Description: This measurement provides the number of intra LTE service based handover attempts. It comprises intra-eNB and inter-eNB handover scenarios.  Service based handovers are used for “traffic steering”, which is to handover UEs with ongoing VoLTE services (QCI1) to specific cells.  An additional use case is the “redirect of VoLTE call setup”, which enables VoLTE call setups through forced service based handovers in cases where VoLTE is not supported by the serving cell.  Note: in case of “traffic steering,” the handover cause “resource optimization handover” (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) (or with equivalent eNB-internal cause) is sent to the handover target cell to initiate the service based handover. Service based handovers triggered due to event A4 reports are counted. Handovers triggered due to event A3/A5 reports are not counted. Load based handover events are not counted either.  Note: In case of “redirect VoLTE call setup,” the handover cause “time critical handover” (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) (or with equivalent eNB-internal cause) is sent to the handover target cell in order to initiate the forced service based handover. Forced service based handovers triggered due to event A3/A4/A5 reports are counted.   Note: In case the LTE2503 feature (Emergency Call based mobility trigger) is enabled, the handover cause "time critical handover" (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) is also counted.

An additional use case is the “redirect of VoLTE call setup”, which enables VoLTE call setups through forced service based handovers in cases where VoLTE is not supported by the serving cell.  Note: in case of “traffic steering,” the handover cause “resource optimization handover” (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) (or with equivalent eNB-internal cause) is sent to the handover target cell to initiate the service based handover. Service based handovers triggered due to event A4 reports are counted. Handovers triggered due to event A3/A5 reports are not counted. Load based handover events are not counted either.  Note: In case of “redirect VoLTE call setup,” the handover cause “time critical handover” (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) (or with equivalent eNB-internal cause) is sent to the handover target cell in order to initiate the forced service based handover. Forced service based handovers triggered due to event A3/A4/A5 reports are counted.   Note: In case the LTE2503 feature (Emergency Call based mobility trigger) is enabled, the handover cause "time critical handover" (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) is also counted.

Note: in case of “traffic steering,” the handover cause “resource optimization handover” (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) (or with equivalent eNB-internal cause) is sent to the handover target cell to initiate the service based handover. Service based handovers triggered due to event A4 reports are counted. Handovers triggered due to event A3/A5 reports are not counted. Load based handover events are not counted either.  Note: In case of “redirect VoLTE call setup,” the handover cause “time critical handover” (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) (or with equivalent eNB-internal cause) is sent to the handover target cell in order to initiate the forced service based handover. Forced service based handovers triggered due to event A3/A4/A5 reports are counted.   Note: In case the LTE2503 feature (Emergency Call based mobility trigger) is enabled, the handover cause "time critical handover" (3GPP TS 36.413, 36.423) is also counted.

4G|M8021C20.Description: This counter provides the number of Late Handovers.  A Late Handover is a sequence of a missed HO attempt (instead of HO, RLF on the UE side and optionally recoverable RLF on the eNB side) in one cell followed by an RRC connection re-establishment request in another cell.   In case of an intra cell handover, this counter shall not be updated. Reason: This MRO-related counter, which is used by the MRO algorithm (LTE533: Mobility Robustness Optimization), is an inter cell handover related counter (that is the handover target cell is different from the handover source cell) which shall not be influenced by intra cell handovers (that is handover target cell is equal to handover source cell).  Note: Handovers for UEs with modified CIO settings are excluded from this counter.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

4G|M8021C20.Updated: Reception of X2AP: RLF INDICATION message satisfying the following conditions: - C-RNTI corresponds to an available UE context - shortMAC-I is included - shortMAC-I matches the local security calculation (successful authentication) - Tstore_UE_cntxt timer associated with the corresponding authenticated shortMAC-I is not running source cell: A cell receiving the X2AP: RLF INDICATION message is received (source cell of missed HO attempt and optional recoverable RLF on eNB side) Target cell:  A cell sending X2AP: RLF INDICATION message  (cell receiving the re-establishment request after missed HO attempt) The counter is incremented at the source cell. Notes: The case of re-establishment cause "ReconfigFailure" is excluded from counting. The case of re-establishment cause "HOfailure" is excluded from counting when the re-establishment target cell is prepared for the incoming HO, as this means the HO has been attempted,  not missed. In case of re-establishment request to the cell prepared for the incoming HO, the case of received PCI being different from the source cell PCI of the prepared HO is excluded from counting. In the source cell of the missed HO attempt, an HO preparation for the considered UE context may be ongoing. The target cell of such HO preparation can be different from the cell receiving the re-establishment request.  In case of an intra cell handover, the counter shall not be updated.

Reason: This MRO-related counter, which is used by the MRO algorithm (LTE533: Mobility Robustness Optimization), is an inter cell handover related counter (that is the handover target cell is different from the handover source cell) which shall not be influenced by intra cell handovers (that is handover target cell is equal to handover source cell).  Note: This counter is not incremented in case the LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

4G|M8021C25.Description: This measurement provides the number of incoming handover preparation attempts irrespective of the handover cause. The counter is updated in the handover target cell for which the incoming handover preparation request was received. The counter is not updated in case of an intra-cell handover. The counter is not updated in case of a RLF (Radio Link Failure) triggered incoming handover.  Remark: The number of incoming handover preparation attempts might be greater than the sum of successful and failed handover preparations because failure counters are only provided for a subset of failure causes.

4G|M8021C43.Description: This counter provides the number of Late Handovers for UEs with modified CIO settings. Note: This counter is not incremented in case the LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

4G|M8021C43.Updated: Reception of X2AP: RLF INDICATION message for UEs with modified CIO settings satisfying the following conditions: - C-RNTI corresponds to an available UE context - shortMAC-I is included - shortMAC-I matches the local security calculation (successful authentication) - Tstore_UE_cntxt timer associated with the corresponding authenticated shortMAC-I is not running source cell: A cell receiving the X2AP: RLF INDICATION message is received (source cell of the missed HO attempt and optional recoverable RLF on eNB side) Target cell:  A cell sending X2AP: RLF INDICATION message  (cell receiving the re-establishment request after the missed HO attempt) The counter is incremented at the source cell. Notes: The case of re-establishment cause "ReconfigFailure" is excluded from counting. The case of re-establishment cause "HOfailure" is excluded from counting when the re-establishment target cell is prepared for the incoming HO, as this means the HO has been attempted, not missed. In case of re-establishment request to the cell prepared for the incoming HO, the case of received PCI being different from the source cell PCI of the prepared HO is excluded from counting. In the source cell of the missed HO attempt, an HO preparation for the considered UE context may be ongoing. The target cell of such HO preparation can be different from the cell receiving the re-establishment request.

Note: SCell (or SCells) is added during HO, that is, SCell configuration done in HO Command (RRC Connection Reconfiguration). In case of "no SCell (or SCells) will be added in HO Cmd", there still is a chance to add SCell (or SCells) at a later time if step-wise SCell addition is enabled.

4G|M8025C1.Description: This measurement provides the number of Failed Inter System Handover preparations to eHRPD caused by expiration of guarding timer TUlHoPrepTransferHrpd per eHRPD bandclass. 4G|M8025C6.Description: This measurement provides the number of Failed Inter System Handover attempts to eHRPD caused by expiration of guarding timer TC2KRelocOverallHRPD per eHRPD bandclass. For each handover relationship between the LTE cell (source of the inter system handover) and the eHRPD bandclass (target of the inter system handover) a separate counter is provided. The timer is started when the eNB sends an RRC:MobilityFromEUTRACommand message to the UE (3GPP TS 36.331) in case that this message is sent for a Inter System Handover to eHRPD. The timer expires when the eNB has not received the corresponding handover related S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message (3GPP TS 36.413) from the MME in time.

The timer is started when the eNB sends an RRC:MobilityFromEUTRACommand message to the UE (3GPP TS 36.331) in case that this message is sent for a Inter System Handover to eHRPD. The timer expires when the eNB has not received the corresponding handover related S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message (3GPP TS 36.413) from the MME in time.

4G|M8026C27.Network Element Name: Total number of failed initial HARQ transmissions in lower PUSCH region on A-MPR-enabled cell in UL
4G|M8026C27.Network Element Name in previous release: Total number of failed initial HARQ transmissions in lower PUSCH region on A-MPR-enabled cell in UL
4G|M8026C27.Description: This counter provides the total number of failed initial HARQ transmissions in the lower PUSCH region on an A-MPR-enabled cell in uplink.  Note1: The lower region consists of all of the PRBs at the lower edge of the allocated UL bandwidth till PUCCH. Note2: In case of interworking with feature LTE4611, the counter does not include the allocations across lower/center/upper PUSCH regions of the single connected UE that is handled by LTE4611 (i.e., counter doesn't include any allocations when UE can use up to 100 PRBs, and in case of PRACH TTI up to a maximum of 64 PRBs, which overlaps with any 2 or 3 PUSCH regions, irrespective of finally allocated PRBs for UE based on available data and PHR). Note3. This counter is not supported with band19_NS08, because there are no lower/center/upper PUSCH regions with feature CB007828.

4G|M8026C39.Description: This counter provides the total number of failed initial HARQ transmissions in the center PUSCH region on an A-MPR-enabled cell in uplink.  Note1: The center region consists of all of the PRBs surrounded by the adjacent PUCCH channels. Note2: In case of interworking with feature LTE4611, the counter does not include the allocations across lower/center/upper PUSCH regions of the single connected UE that is handled by LTE4611 (i.e., counter doesn't include any allocations when UE can use up to 100 PRBs, and in case of PRACH TTI up to a maximum of 64 PRBs, which overlaps with any 2 or 3 PUSCH regions, irrespective of finally allocated PRBs for UE based on available data and PHR). Note3. This counter is not supported with band19_NS08 because there are no lower/center/upper PUSCH regions with feature CB007828.

4G|M8032C0.Description: This measurement represents the number of times a UE was in the process of being handed over from LTE to UTRAN for any reason (e.g. CSFB, PSHO, Load Balancing) and encountered a handover failure when attempting to acquire the UTRAN cell.  The LTE system identifies an “early handover” using certain information in the UE Context (see also section “Updated” for the counter trigger description).  In this case, the B2 threshold2 measurement threshold for PSHO was met.  The counter is updated in the handover source cell (LTE cell) with separate counters for each UTRAN (WCDMA or TD-SCDMA) frequency.  This counter only applies when LTE1749 (MRO Inter-RAT UTRAN) and either LTE56 (PSHO to WCDMA) or LTE898 (PSHO to TD-SCDMA) are activated.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

4G|M8032C0.Updated: This counter is updated following the reception of an RRC: UEInformationResponse or X2AP: RLF INDICATION (or internal eNB RLF Indication message) containing the RLF-Report information element where all conditions as listed below are met. Meeting these conditions means that the configured B2 threshold2 measurement threshold for PSHO to UTRAN (RSCP or EcN0 based on configuration) was set to a value which would not have resulted in a handover to UTRAN being initiated based on the measurements of the UTRAN neighbor cells.   - LTE1749 and either LTE56 or LTE898 are activated - RLF-Report.selectedUTRA-CellId is included  - RLF-Report.timeConnFailure is not included, or it is included and RLF-Report.timeConnFailure > timeConnFailureThreshold - taking into account the units of each (This means that there is no recent incoming handover for the UE prior to the RLF event.).   - RLF-Report.timeSinceFailure reflects a time that is more recent than the mroAdjustmentTimestamp (non-persistent parameter) - taking into account the units of each (This means that RLF events which occurred prior to a handover parameter configuration change are not counted.).  - RLF-Report.connectionFailureType = "rlf" - RLF-Report.measResultListUTRA-r9 is included and contains a measurement for the cell identified by RLF-Report.selectedUTRA-CellId and for the configured measQuantityUtra - the strongest included measurement for the selectedUTRA-CellId's UTRAN frequency and applicable measurement quantity is weaker than the configured threshold, as determined below:          - if measQuantityUtra = 0 (RSCP) for WCDMA, or if this is TD-SCDMA              - for the UTRAN frequency identified in selectedUTRA-CellId, the strongest measResultListUTRA.rscp (if included) <= b2Threshold2UtraRscp + (hysB2ThresholdUtra*2) - offsetFreqUtra (from LNHOW for WCDMA or LNHOT for TD-SCDMA)           - else (this is WCDMA and measQuantityUtra = 1 (EcN0))                   - for the UTRAN frequency identified in selectedUTRA-CellId, the strongest measResultListUTRA.EcN0 (if included) <= b2Threshold2UtraEcn0 + (hysB2ThresholdUtra*2) - offsetFreqUtra (from LNHOW)  - the serving cell RSRP measurement is weaker than the configured B2T1 threshold (that is B2T1 has been met), as determined below: -	RLF-Report.measResultLastServCell.rsrpResult < b2Threshold1Utra - (hysB2ThresholdUtra *2) (from LNHOW for WCDMA or LNHOT for TD-SCDMA)  The counter is incremented against: - Cell - RLF-Report.failedPCellId  - UTRAN frequency - UTRAN (WCDMA or TD-SCDMA) frequency associated with RLF-Report.selectedUTRA-CellId

4G|M8032C1.Description: This measurement represents the number of times a UE was connected in LTE, then experienced a Radio Link Failure (RLF) in LTE, then selected UTRAN to re-connect to, and then re-connected again to the LTE system which identified a “late handover” using certain RLF report information transmitted from the UE to the eNB (see also section “Updated” for the counter trigger description). In this case, the UE was measuring the target UTRAN frequency (that is B1 or B2 measurement was activated for any reason), but the B2 threshold2 measurement threshold for VoLTE was not met.  Note that this counter can only be triggered by 3GPP Release 11 (or higher) UEs as the RRC RLF Report information used to detect this use case was added in Release 11 (selectedUTRAN-CellId IE).  Also note that the eNB cannot determine which measurement was actually activated at the UE (B1 for CSFB, B1 for Load Balancing, B2 for PSHO, or B2 for VoLTE).  The counter is updated in the LTE cell where RLF occurred with separate counters for each UTRAN (WCDMA) frequency.  This counter only applies when LTE1749 (MRO Inter-RAT UTRAN) and LTE56 (PSHO to WCDMA) and LTE64 (Service based handover thresholds) are activated.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

4G|M8032C1.Counter Description: This measurement represents the number of times a UE was connected in LTE, then experienced a Radio Link Failure (RLF) in LTE, then selected UTRAN to re-connect to, and then re-connected again to the LTE system which identified a “late handover” using certain RLF report information transmitted from the UE to the eNB (see also section “Updated” for the counter trigger description). In this case, the UE was measuring the target UTRAN frequency (that is B1 or B2 measurement was activated for any reason), but the B2 threshold2 measurement threshold for VoLTE was not met.  Note that this counter can only be triggered by 3GPP Release 11 (or higher) UEs as the RRC RLF Report information used to detect this use case was added in Release 11 (selectedUTRAN-CellId IE).  Also note that the eNB cannot determine which measurement was actually activated at the UE (B1 for CSFB, B1 for Load Balancing, B2 for PSHO, or B2 for VoLTE).  The counter is updated in the LTE cell where RLF occurred with separate counters for each UTRAN (WCDMA) frequency.  This counter only applies when LTE1749 (MRO Inter-RAT UTRAN) and LTE56 (PSHO to WCDMA) and LTE64 (Service based handover thresholds) are activated.  Note: This counter is not incremented in case LTE5603 is enabled and the given UE Context has been triggered earlier by SPID based handover, just before related MRO re-establishment, RLF Indication or Handover Report event was received.

The counter DENOM_RRC_CONN_UE_PLMN can be used by NetAct as a denominator to calculate the average number of RRC-connected UEs per PLMN via SUM_RRC_CONN_UE_PLMN/DENOM_RRC_CONN_UE_PLMN. Notes: The UE informs the eNB during RRC connection establishment to which PLMN the UE is connected. The PLMN may be changed during handover.

4G|M8038C67.Description: This counter provides the mean QCI 65 E-RAB setup time per PLMN ID.
4G|M8038C67.Description in previous release: This counter provides the mean QCI 65 E-RAB setup time per PLMN ID.
4G|M8038C67.Updated: This counter is updated by accumulating the time intervals for every successfully established QCI 65 E-RAB per PLMN ID between the reception of an E-RAB SETUP REQUEST or INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST message and the transmission of the corresponding E-RAB SETUP RESPONSE or INITIAL CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE message by the eNB over the granularity period. The end value of this time will then be divided by the number of successfully established E-RABs in the granularity period to give the arithmetic mean. The counter is reinitialized at the beginning of each granularity period. Note: The counter is initialized with "0" at the beginning of each granularity period. A counter result "0" at the end of the granularity period (for example, 15 minutes) means that no E-RAB setup occurred in the cell during the whole granularity period and that the counter does not contain a valid counter result.

4G|M8046C4.Description: This counter provides the maximum retention period for a PDCP SDU (DL) matching the respective PMQAP Profile inside the eNB. Retention delay is measured for each PDCP SDU matching the respective PMQAP Profile. The measurement starts at the reception of a PDCP SDU on the PDCP layer and ends at the first TB transmission on the MAC layer including the PDCP SDU or the first segment of it.   Note: The PDCP, RLC, MAC protocols processing, and DL scheduling delay are included in the counter calculation. The DL scheduling delay is the dominant factor in the counter value.  In case of FDD Inter-band/Intra-band Carrier Aggregation with Two Flexi Zone Micro BTSs (LTE1858), this counter is applicable only to PCell traffic, that is, the SCell data is excluded.

4G|M8047C0.Updated: The volume of a data burst excluding the data transmitted in the TTI when the buffer is emptied. A sample for ThpVolDl is the data volume, counted on PDCP SDU level in bits, successfully transmitted (acknowledged by the UE) in DL for the respective PMQAP Profile during a sample of ThpTimeDl. It must exclude the volume of the last piece of data emptying the buffer. Note: Please check the LTE5077 feature description for detailed information on counter pegging mechanism.

4G|M8047C22.Updated: This counter is triggered according to 3GPP TS 36.314 with the fraction of TTI of single TTI bursts of the ERABs in the PMQAP Profile calculated as follows:  ThpTimeDl=TTI*(TBVol-PaddingVol)/TBVol  Where:   1. TTI is the duration of the TTI. 2. TBVol is the Volume of the TB related to one TTI burst and represents UE achievable TB size. 3. PaddingVol is the Volume of padding bits added into Transport Block related to one TTI burst. TBVol-PaddingVol is an MAC PDU volume to which the bearer specific PDCP SDU volume of the single TTI burst is mapped in the MAC layer excluding padding bits.
