4G|M8048C2.Description: This counter provides the number of released E-RABs with normal release cause per the respective PMQAP Profile.  Normal releases are due to user inactivity, UE redirection, successful ISHO, normal call end, or due to the Detach procedure.   Note: The E-RAB releases due to successful intra-LTE HO are also perceived as normal releases, but they are excluded from this counter in order to be consistent with the existing E-RAB KPIs.
4G|M8048C2.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of released E-RABs with normal release cause per the respective PMQAP Profile.  Normal releases are due to user inactivity, UE redirection, successful ISHO, normal call end, or due to the Detach procedure.   Note: The E-RAB releases due to successful intra-LTE HO are also perceived as normal releases, but they are excluded from this counter in order to be consistent with the existing E-RAB KPIs.
4G|M8048C2.Updated: Release initiated by the eNB:   S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message with the RNL cause "User Inactivity" sent by the eNB to the MME.   S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message sent by the eNB to the MME with the RNL causes "Inter-RAT redirection", "Redirection towards 1xRTT", "CS Fallback Triggered", "UE Not Available For PS Service", or "E-UTRAN Generated Reason" if the release cause is set due to an intra-LTE redirect.  Release initiated by the EPC:  Reception of an S1AP:E-RAB RELEASE COMMAND or an S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message sent by the MME to the eNB due to "NAS: Normal release" or the Detach procedure.   The counter is not incremented in case that the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND is received as a response to a previously sent S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST.  Inter-system:  HO to UTRAN with SRVCC or HO to GERAN with SRVCC or PS-HO to UTRAN or HO to SA NR: Following the reception of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message with the cause "RNL Successful Handover", the counter is incremented with the number of bearers admitted by the HO target of the preceding HO preparation procedure. The bearers, which are not admitted, are contained in the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the  S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND  message that is received from the MME (3GPP TS 36.413 / 38.413).

4G|M8048C3.Description: This counter provides the number of released E-RABs with abnormal release cause for active UEs (having data in the buffer) per the respective PMQAP Profile.  Note: The E-RAB releases due to successful intra-LTE HO are also perceived as normal releases, but they are not counted in either normal or in abnormal release counter in order to be consistent with the existing E-RAB KPIs.  Note: Multiple bearers, matching the same profile, are counted separately in the same profile.  One bearer matching multiple profiles is counted separately in all matching profiles.  Note: An abnormal release leads to an unwanted release of an E-RAB.

4G|M8048C3.Updated: Upon abnormal release of an ERAB for UEs having data in the buffer by the eNB matching the respective PMQAP Profile. The following are considered to be abnormal releases: Partial handover through S1:  1. not admitted bearers from the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message are counted only in case when the cause code from the given message is NOT "successful-handover", and  2. after S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND reception the S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message must be received with RNL cause "Successful Handover". 4G|M8048C3.Counter Description: This counter provides the number of released E-RABs with abnormal release cause for active UEs (having data in the buffer) per the respective PMQAP Profile. 4G|M8048C9.Updated: Updated: The counter is updated when HO preparation is completed.  Intra-eNB HO: The reception of the eNB-internal Handover Request Acknowledge message.  Inter -eNB HO through X2 The reception of an X2AP: Handover Request Acknowledge message from the target eNB.  Inter-eNB HO through S1: The reception of an S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message from the MME to the source eNB.   Intra-eNB HO: This counter is incremented with the number of bearers admitted for the target cell. The admitted bearers are contained in the eNB-internal message representing the successful outcome of the preceding eNB-internal HO preparation procedure.  Inter-eNB HO through X2: This counter is incremented with the number of bearers admitted by the target eNB during the preceding HO preparation procedure. The admitted bearers are contained in the "E-RABs Admitted List" IE of the X2AP:HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message that is received from the target eNB (3GPP TS 36.423).  Inter-eNB HO through S1: This counter is incremented with the number of bearers admitted by the HO target during the preceding HO preparation procedure. The bearers, which are not admitted, are contained in the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND message that is received from the MME (3GPP TS 36.413).

4G|M8048C20.Updated: Upon abnormal release of an ERAB by the eNB matching the respective PMQAP Profile. The following are considered to be abnormal releases: Partial handover through S1:  1. not admitted bearers from the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message are counted only in case when the cause code from the given message is NOT "successful-handover", and  2. after S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND reception the S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message must be received with RNL cause "Successful Handover".  Partial handover through X2 - not admitted bearers from the "E-RABs Not Admitted List" of the X2AP: HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message when X2AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE message is received. eNB-initiated E-RAB release - S1AP: E-RAB RELEASE INDICATION is sent.  eNB-initiated UE context release due to a reason other than user inactivity or UE redirect - S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with the RNL cause other than "User Inactivity", "Inter-RAT redirection", "Redirection towards 1xRTT", "CS Fallback Triggered", "UE Not Available For PS Service" or "E-UTRAN Generated Reason" is sent (Remark: S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with "E-UTRAN Generated Reason" RNL cause can also be sent due to a procedure other than UE redirect and such should be considered as an abnormal case).  MME-initiated E-RAB or UE context release due to a reason other than normal call end or detach procedure - S1AP: E-RAB RELEASE COMMAND or S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND with NAS cause other than "Normal release" or "Detach" is received.  Failed path switch - bearers for which path switch failed from the "E-RAB To Be Released List" of the received S1AP: PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLDEGE message.  Exceptions are the ERABs when the ERAB Release command was already sent previously for the same UE.  S1 Setup, Reset or Link failure - RRC: RRC CONNECTION RELEASE is sent due to the S1 Setup, Reset or Link Failure procedures.  X2 Reset - LTE UEC receives UEC_X2L3AvailabilityChangeReq message with status "unavailable".

4G|M8048C44.Description in previous release: This measurement provides the number of E-RABs that are abnormally released due to the expiration of the HO Guard Timer for an "intra-LTE HO", "inter-system HO to UTRAN", "inter-system HO to SA NR", "SRVCC to UTRAN", or "SRVCC to GSM". The counter is maintained in the source cell for E-RABs per the respective PMQAP Profile.
4G|M8048C44.Updated: This counter is updated following the transmission of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message to the MME due to the expiration of the Handover Guard Timer for outgoing "intra-LTE HO", "inter-system HO to UTRAN", "SRVCC to UTRAN", or "SRVCC to GSM", "inter-system HO to SA NR".  Intra-eNB HO: Upon the transmission of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message to the MME due to the expiration of the Handover Guard Timer THOoverall, the counter is incremented with the number of bearers admitted during the preceding HO preparation procedure. The admitted bearers are contained in the eNB internal message representing the "Handover Request Acknowledge".  Inter-eNB HO via X2: Upon the transmission of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message to the MME due to the expiration of the Handover Guard Timer TX2RELOCoverall, the counter is incremented with the number of bearers admitted by the target eNB during the preceding HO preparation procedure. The admitted bearers are contained in the "E-RABs Admitted List" IE of the X2AP:HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message that is received from the target eNB (3GPP TS 36.423).  Inter-eNB HO via S1 / Inter-system HO to UTRAN / SRVCC to UTRAN / Inter-system HO to SA NR: Upon the transmission of the S1AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST message to the MME due to the expiration of the Handover Guard Timer TS1RELOCoverall, the counter is incremented with the number of bearers admitted by the HO target during the preceding HO preparation procedure. The bearers, which are not admitted, are contained in the "E-RABs to Release List" IE of the S1AP:HANDOVER COMMAND message that is received from MME (3GPP TS 36.413 / 38.413).

4G|M8051C17.Description: This counter provides the average number of DL CA-capable UEs for four component carriers (4 CCs) in the current cell. This counter is updated in the PCell.   The reported value is 100 times higher than the actual value (for example, 1.00 is stored as 100). Note: If a UE supports 2 CCs and 3CCs as well, this is counted in M8051C121 and M8051C122, separately. Additionally, in case that the skipFallback function is in use (IE "eNB-RequestedParameters-r13 -> skipFallbackCombRequested-r13" is set to true), each lower CC counter is pegged as well, regardless whether the aforementioned CC combinations are present inside the UE Capability Information or not.
4G|M8051C17.Description in previous release: This counter provides the average number of DL CA-capable UEs for four component carriers (4 CCs) in the current cell. Note: If a UE supports 2 CCs and 3CCs as well, this is counted in M8051C121 and M8051C122, separately. Additionally, in case that the skipFallback function is in use (IE "eNB-RequestedParameters-r13 -> skipFallbackCombRequested-r13" is set to true), each lower CC counter is pegged as well, regardless whether the aforementioned CC combinations are present inside the UE Capability Information or not.
4G|M8051C17.Updated: This counter is updated by the arithmetical average of samples taken from those UEs that are DL CA-capable for four component carriers.  Note: CA Capability is checked based on the UE Capability Information message received by the eNB from the UE, and it is not cross-checked with the CA configuration set of the eNB.

This counter, divided by the denominator DENOM_ACTIVE_UE_SCHED_DATA_UL, provides the average number of active UEs per cell, which had data scheduled. in UL.
4G|M8051C103.Description in previous release: This measurement provides sum of scheduled UEs with expected DRB data in UL per cell to measure the number of simultaneously Active UEs in a TTI, which had data scheduled in UL.  This counter, divided by the denominator DENOM_ACTIVE_UE_SCHED_DATA_UL, provides the average number of active UEs per cell, which had data scheduled. in UL.
4G|M8051C103.Updated: This counter is incremented by each UL grant for which the eNB expects a UE to use for the transmission of the DRB data. The actually received UL data is not considered for the counter. Note: The eNB has to make certain assumptions depending on the cause for the allocated UL grants due to: - LCG level UL BSR delivery (no bearer level accuracy);  - nature of the SR mechanism (no information about data type in buffer); and - other uncertainties These assumptions are listed below in detail.  This counter is incremented if the UL grant for the SR is assigned and if the eNB assumes that DRB data will be sent. This is also true if the UE does not actually send any data using the assigned grant. This counter is not incremented in case of: - The UL grant for the UE reporting only LCG0 data transmission in UE buffers. This also applies in case QCI5 DRB is mapped to LCG0; - The UL grant to a UE without the reception of a positive SR or without the reception of a BSR indication data in buffer (proactive UL scheduling); - The UL grant for RA msg3/1st scheduled UL transmission after RA response/msg2 - The UL grant for SR if a UL SRB message is expected.

4G|M8051C150.Description: This counter provides the maximum number of EN-DC UEs with at least one SCG split bearer configured at the PCell (source cell).
4G|M8051C150.Description in previous release: This counter provides the maximum number of EN-DC UEs with at least one SCG split bearer configured at the PCell (source cell).
4G|M8051C150.Updated: This measurement is obtained by sampling the number of EN-DC DC UEs with at least one configured SCG split bearer at a predefined interval (1 sec) and updating it if the current value is higher than the already stored maximum value. The SCG split bearer is considered as configured for an EN-DC UE when eNB (source cell for the purpose of this counter) received RRC Connection Reconfiguration Complete message from the UE: 1. If the previous SgNB Addition preparation procedure was successful - SgNB Addition Request Acknowledge with IE ‘E-RABs-Admitted-ToBeAdded List’ contains at least one admitted SCG split bearer. 2. If the previous SgNB Modification procedure was successful - SgNB Modification Request Acknowledge with either IE 'E-RABs-Admitted-ToBeAdded-List’ or 'E-RABs-Admitted-ToBeModified-List’ or 'E-RABs-Admitted-ToBeReleased-List’ contains at least one admitted (or sustained in case of modified and released lists) SCG split bearer.  Note: If RRC Connection Reconfiguration message with ‘HO Command’ is sent to the UE from the eNB then the UE is treated as if it would have been released, only if the source cell does not expect to receive RRC Connection Reconfiguration Complete message, and is not considered for counter incrementation during the sampling time interval which takes part after the given message is sent.

4G|M8056C0.Description: This counter measures the uplink Received Interference Power (RIP) mean value for PRB 0, measured in the eNB.  Note regarding LTE3464: In case of UL MU-MIMO and massive MIMO combined together, the uplink RIP for PRBs is the total of average I+N (interference power) for each PRB in 100 ms.  The average I+N for each PRB is the total of I+N from the available layers for each PRB divided by the number of available layers for each PRB.
4G|M8056C0.Description in previous release: This counter measures the uplink Received Interference Power (RIP) mean value for PRB 0, measured in the eNB.  Note regarding LTE3464: In case of UL MU-MIMO and massive MIMO combined together, the uplink RIP for PRBs is the total of average I+N (interference power) for each PRB in 100 ms.  The average I+N for each PRB is the total of I+N from the available layers for each PRB divided by the number of available layers for each PRB.
4G|M8056C0.Updated: This counter is updated within the measurement period with the arithmetical average value of samples, each sample presenting the average RIP in the uplink subframe over 100 ms for PRB 0.  Note for FDD: Artificial value of -130dBm is used to cover RA msg3s to ghost preambles as well as any other cases where UE does not send UL transmission or sent UL transmission is not detected.

Note regarding LTE3464: In case of UL MU-MIMO and massive MIMO combined together, the uplink RIP for PRBs is the total of average I+N (interference power) for each PRB in 100 ms. Note: LTE2235 TIME_RACH_ACB depends on "acbNumSteps" and "acbUpdateTimer" parameters, as well as ongoing traffic loads. Because of those specific conditions, there might be a difference between the values of counters TIME_ACB_RACH (M8057C8) and TIME_ACB_ALL (M8057C2). An example of this specific condition is when RACH burst triggers Access Class Barring, but, after a while, the RACH load decreases to normal level.

Notes: The eNB has to make certain assumptions depending on the cause for the allocated UL grants due to: - the LCG level UL BSR delivery (no bearer level accuracy) - the nature of the SR mechanism (no information about data type in buffer) - other uncertainties  These assumptions are listed below in detail:  This counter is incremented if the UL grant for the SR is assigned and if the eNB assumes that the DRB data is to be sent. This counter is not incremented in case of: - the UL grant for the UE is reporting only LCG0 data transmission in UE buffers. 4G|M8061C61.Network Element Name in previous release: Number of MME Initiated UE Context Release Command due to detected double S1 for LTE-M UEs
4G|M8061C61.Description: This counter provides the number of released UE Contexts due to Double S1 scenario, both before and after default E-RAB establishment.   This counter is updated only for LTE-M UEs.

4G|M8061C61.Updated: This counter is updated when UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message is received from the MME with cause = 'Radio Connection with UE Lost', and no UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST has been sent to the MME previously for a LTE-M UE.  This counter is updated for LTE-M.  Note: 'Double S1' in intra-LTE mobility context is resulted from a loss of radio link due to poor RF channel conditions. A connected UE can move over to another eNodeB without successfully requesting handover to the serving cell due to a sudden change in RF conditions. From UE's perspective, this is a Radio Link Failure. And it is referred to as double S1 because when the UE performs TAU on the new eNB, MME senses an existing S1 connection for the UE with the old serving eNB and thus sends CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND to release it.

4G|M8061C148.Description: This counter provides the number of E-RABs released due to the partial HO. 4G|M8061C148.Updated: Inter-eNB HO through X2: Following the reception of the X2AP:UE CONTEXT RELEASE message, this counter is incremented with the number of bearers not admitted by the target eNB of the preceding HO preparation procedure. The bearers, which are not admitted, are included in the "E-RABs Not Admitted List" IE of the X2AP:HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message that is received from the target eNB (3GPP TS 36.423).  This counter is only updated for LTE-M.

4G|M8061C192.Network Element Name: Uplink grant size weighted new Tx repetition distribution for CatM - 1 repetition (LTE-M)
4G|M8061C192.Network Element Name in previous release: Uplink grant size weighted new Tx repetition distribution for CatM - 1 repetition (LTE-M)
4G|M8061C192.Description: This counter provides the weighted number of PRBs assigned when M-PUSCH repetitions are set to 1 for a new packet transmission (excluding msg3) made in TxDiv or SIMO mode issued by dynamic scheduler for Cat-M UE.   The weight is the number of M-PUSCH PRBs assigned for the first transmission of the repetition. For example, for repetitions set to 2, there can be 12 PRBs used in total, but only 6 are used for the calculation.   This counter excludes HARQ retransmitted packets.  Note: The secondary NB is taken into account.

4G|M8061C216.Network Element Name in previous release: Maximum number of VoLTE capable UEs (LTE-M)

Note: This counter is used only for LTE-M.
4G|M8061C244.Updated: This counter is updated in each TTI with the number of active Cat-M UEs that had data scheduled in UL on the second NB. This counter is incremented by each UL grant for which the eNB expects a Cat-M UE to use for the transmission of the DRB data. The actual received UL data is not considered for this counter.   Note: The eNB has to make certain assumptions depending on the cause for the allocated UL grants due to: a.	the LCG level UL BSR delivery (no bearer level accuracy) b.	the nature of the SR mechanism (no information about data type in buffer) c.	other uncertainties  These assumptions are listed below in detail.   This counter is incremented: a.	if the UL grant for the SR is assigned, and if the eNB assumes that the DRB data will be sent. This is also true if the UE does not actually send any data using the assigned grant. b.	 in case of repetitions  This counter is not incremented in case that: a.	the UL grant for the UE is reporting only LCG0 data transmission in UE buffers. This also applies in case QCI5 DRB is mapped to LCG0. b.	the UL grant is to a UE without the reception of a positive SR or without the reception of a BSR indication data in buffer (proactive UL scheduling). c.	the UL grant is for a scheduled UL transmission of an RA msg3/1st scheduled UL transmission after an RA response/msg2. d.	the UL grant is for an SR if a UL SRB message is expected.  Note: This counter is only updated for LTE-M UEs.

4G|M8061C247.Network Element Name: The percentage of unsuppressed OFDM symbols with micro DTX to all transmitted symbols in FS module due to LTE-M related activities
4G|M8061C247.Network Element Name in previous release: The percentage of unsuppressed OFDM symbols with micro DTX to all transmitted symbols in FS module due to LTE-M related activities
4G|M8061C247.Description: This counter provides the percentage of unsuppressed OFDM symbols with micro DTX to all transmitted symbols in FS module due to LTE-M-related activities (RA procedure, LTE-M UE in RRC connected state, Paging procedure, Direct Indication sending,  SIBx-BR [x>1] sending). 4G|M8066C16.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of concurrently used NB-IoT subcarriers in UL, which are measured during an interval of one millisecond and accumulated over the measurement period.
4G|M8066C16.Updated: This counter is updated after each 1 ms interval, in which UL resources for NB-IoT UEs were used. It is incremented by the number of subcarriers (granularity of 3.75 kHz) used in parallel by any NB-IoT UE. (15 kHz subcarriers result in an increment of 4 per interval).  Note: In case of NB-IoT inband mode, this 1 ms interval corresponds to a subframe of the hosting WB cell, that is, a subframe containing one or more host PRBs allocated to NB-IoT UEs. These PRBs are considered unusable from host cell perspective.

4G|M8080C59.Description in previous release: This counter provides the average number of UEs with a configured SCG split bearer and at least one activated SCell for CA purposes at the PCell.
4G|M8080C59.Updated: This counter is obtained by sampling the number of UEs with a configured SCG split bearer and with at least one SCell activated at a predefined interval (1s), and then adding up these sample values over the measurement period and dividing them with the measurement time duration. The reported value is 100 times higher than the actual value (for example 1.00 is stored as 100).  Note1: The UE with a configured SCG split bearer is understood when the bearer has been changed from MCG to SCG split type, which happens during SgNB Addition or SgNB Modification procedure after the serving cell receives the RRC Connection Reconfiguration Complete message from the UE.  Note2: The UE has an SCell activated whenever MAC PS changes its state from configured, which happens based on traffic-related O&M parameters and current UE traffic needs.  Note3: The UE that fulfills the conditions but its connection is not long enough to fall into sampling periodicity is not taken into calculation.

4G|M8080C128.Description in previous release: This counter provides the sum of time taken for successful SgNB addition for sampled EN-DC activated UEs.  This counter, divided by the denominator SGNB_ADD_SUCC_DENOM, provides the average time for successful SgNB addition.
4G|M8080C128.Updated: This counter calculates the sum of total time taken by EN-DC activated UE for successful addition of SgNB.  The time calculated between start and end duration is as below: - Time starts when the MeNB sends the "X2AP: SgNB Addition Request" message to the SgNB. - Time ends when the MeNB receives the "S1AP: E-RAB Modification Confirm" message from the MME and it was accepted by the MeNB as a consistent answer, which acknowledges successful SgNB addition due to the completion of the SgNB Addition procedure. Note: Successful SgNB addition is acknowledged with at least one SCG Split Bearer included in the E-RAB Modify List IE.

4G|M8080C142.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of B1-NR reports triggering the NR-reportCGI procedure for an unknown PCI.
4G|M8080C142.Updated: This counter is updated when the RRC Measurement Report message is received from the UE for the B1-NR measurement type, which triggers addition of the reported NR PCI to the NR CGI verification list of pending NR-reportCGI measurements. A single report contains a maximum of eight entries and the counter is incremented for each NR PCI that meets the above condition. It is used to have evidence of how many unknown detected NR neighbor cells are candidates for confirmation by the reportStrongestCells measurement and resolved by the NR-reportCGI measurement, and to have a basis for a metric evaluation of how many unknown NR neighbor cells are confirmed by the reportStrongestCells measurement. The counter is also updated when NR-PCI/NR-Carrier is added to the NR CGI verification list of pending NR-reportCGI measurements, due to a re-verification of the corresponding LNRELGNBCELL.

4G|M8080C155.Network Element Name: Inter-Frequency EN-DC capability based Handover Execution successes to preferred layer
4G|M8080C155.Description: This counter provides the number of Inter-Frequency EN-DC capability based Handover Execution successes to the preferred layer.  Note: The Intra-Cell Handover and RLF triggered Handovers are excluded from this counter.
4G|M8080C155.Updated: This counter is updated for Intra-eNB, Inter-eNB X2, and S1 scenarios when Inter-Frequency EN-DC capability based Handover Execution to the preferred layer is successful. For Intra-eNB, the internal eNB trigger is used. For Inter-eNB X2, the X2AP: UE Context Release message is used. For Inter-eNB S1, the S1AP: UE Context Release Command message is used.  It's pegged from the EN-DC capable layer to the EN-DC preferred layer only. It's NOT pegged when the UE is moved from the EN-DC non-capable layer to EN-DC capable layer.  Note: This counter is updated to the source cell.
4G|M8080C155.Related to Feature: CB007163: EN-DC capability based handover to preferred layer
4G|M8080C155.Counter Description: This counter provides the number of Inter-Frequency EN-DC capability based Handover Execution successes to the preferred layer.  Note: The Intra-Cell Handover and RLF triggered Handovers are excluded from this counter.

4G|M8080C156.Description: This counter provides the number of Inter-Frequency EN-DC capability based Handover Execution attempts to the preferred layer.   Note: The Intra-Cell Handover and RLF triggered Handovers are excluded from this counter.
4G|M8080C156.Updated: This counter is updated for Intra-eNB, Inter-eNB X2, and S1 scenarios when Inter-Frequency EN-DC capability based Handover Execution to the preferred layer is started. For Intra-eNB, Inter-eNB X2, and Inter-eNB S1 the RRC Connection Reconfiguration message with Handover Command is used, which is sent from the eNB to the UE.   It's pegged from EN-DC capable layer to EN-DC preferred layer only. It's NOT pegged when the UE is moved from EN-DC non-capable layer to EN-DC capable layer.  Note: This counter is updated to the source cell.

4G|M8088C0.Description: This counter provides the maximum transmit power in milliwatt at the end of the collection interval.  Note1: The counter is using a fixed inner and configurable outer sliding window with the eirpAvgWinLen parameter. Note2: Calculation algorithms of counters MAX_PWR_DL_EIRP_CTRL and MAX_TRANS_PWR use different collection, sampling, and processing times. Therefore, values of these counters can be different, and thus cannot be compared directly.
4G|M8088C0.Description in previous release: This counter provides the maximum transmit power in milliwatt at the end of the collection interval.  Note1: The counter is using a fixed inner and configurable outer sliding window with the eirpAvgWinLen parameter. Note2: Calculation algorithms of counters MAX_PWR_DL_EIRP_CTRL and MAX_TRANS_PWR use different collection, sampling, and processing times. Therefore, values of these counters can be different, and thus cannot be compared directly.
4G|M8088C0.Updated: This counter is updated with the maximum sample for transmitted power (in milliwatt).   Each sample is a function of the previous samples contained in the outer sliding window as follows: 1. The samples in the outer sliding windows are calculated as an average from the TTIs contained in the inner sliding window. 2. The sample with the maximum value from all samples in the outer sliding window is selected.

4G|M8094C321.Description: This counter provides the average EIRP in the cell segment 15 (in milliwatts) at the end of the collection interval.  Note: The counter is using a fixed inner and configurable outer sliding window with the eirpAvgWinLen parameter.
4G|M8094C321.Updated: This counter is updated at the end of the measurement period with the average of all the samples for EIRP in the cell segment 15 (in milliwatts). The samples in the outer sliding windows are calculated as an average from the TTIs contained in the inner sliding window. 2. The average is calculated from all of the samples contained in the outer sliding window.

4G|M8094C399.Product Type: AirScale SBTS,ASM FDD,ASM TDD,Flexi SBTS,FSM-r3 FDD,FSM-r3 TDD
4G|M8094C399.Description: This counter provides the number of samples when the transmitted power by the eNB wasn't limited due to the EIRP control in the cell segment 32 because of the heavy volume of HARQ retransmissions or Common Channel transmissions.  If eirpSetGbrOverEirp is set to 'true', then the GBR traffic isn't limited and can also trigger this counter.
4G|M8094C399.Updated: This counter is updated in each sample from the cell segment 32 when the transmitted power by the eNB wasn't limited due to priority services, or due to the heavy HARQ volume or Control Channel transmissions.  If eirpSetGbrOverEirp is set to 'true', then the GBR traffic isn't limited and can also trigger this counter.  This counter, divided by DEN_DL_EIRP_CTRL_SEG, provides the percentage of time in the measurement period when the EIRP control isn't limiting transmission power in the cell segment 32 due to exceptional cases.

4G|M8101C7.Description: This counter provides the number of released VoLTE E-RABs for IMS emergency session with abnormal release cause.  Note: The E-RAB releases due to successful intra-LTE HO are also perceived as normal releases, but they are not counted in either normal or in abnormal release counter in order to be consistent with the existing E-RAB KPIs.  Note: An abnormal release means a release that leads to an unwanted release of an ERAB.
4G|M8101C7.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of released VoLTE E-RABs for IMS emergency session with abnormal release cause.  Note: The E-RAB releases due to successful intra-LTE HO are also perceived as normal releases, but they are not counted in either normal or in abnormal release counter in order to be consistent with the existing E-RAB KPIs.  Note: An abnormal release means a release that leads to an unwanted release of an ERAB.
4G|M8101C7.Updated: This counter is updated upon abnormal release of a VoLTE ERAB for IMS emergency session by the eNB. The following are considered abnormal releases: 1. Partial handover through S1 - not admitted bearers from the "E-RABs to Release List" of the S1AP: HANDOVER COMMAND message when S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message with RNL cause "Successful Handover" is received. 2. Partial handover through X2 - not admitted bearers from the "E-RABs Not Admitted List" of the X2AP: HANDOVER REQUEST ACKNOWLEDGE message when X2AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE message is received. 3. eNB initiated E-RAB release - S1AP: E-RAB RELEASE INDICATION is sent. 4. eNB-initiated UE context release due to reason other than user inactivity or UE redirect - S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with the RNL cause other than "User Inactivity", "Inter-RAT redirection", "Redirection towards 1xRTT", "CS Fallback Triggered", "UE Not Available For PS Service", or "E-UTRAN Generated Reason" is sent (Remark: S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST with "E-UTRAN Generated Reason" RNL cause can be also sent due to procedure other than UE redirect. Such should be considered as abnormal case.). 5. MME-initiated E-RAB or UE context release due to reason other than normal call end or detach procedure - S1AP: E-RAB RELEASE COMMAND or S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND with NAS cause other than "Normal release" or "Detach" is received. 6. Failed path switch - bearers for which path switch failed from the "E-RAB To Be Released List" of the received S1AP: PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLDEGE message. 7. S1 Setup, Reset or Link failure - RRC: RRC CONNECTION RELEASE is sent due to S1 Setup, Reset or Link Failure procedures. 8. X2 Reset - LTE UEC receives UEC_X2L3AvailabilityChangeReq message with status "unavailable".
4G|M8101C7.Updated in previous release: This counter is updated upon abnormal release of a VoLTE ERAB for IMS emergency session by the eNB. The following are considered abnormal releases: 1. Such should be considered as abnormal case.). 5. MME-initiated E-RAB or UE context release due to reason other than normal call end or detach procedure - S1AP: E-RAB RELEASE COMMAND or S1AP: UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND with NAS cause other than "Normal release" or "Detach" is received. 6. Failed path switch - bearers for which path switch failed from the "E-RAB To Be Released List" of the received S1AP: PATH SWITCH ACKNOWLDEGE message. 7. Note: "Double S1" in intra-LTE mobility context is a result of a loss of radio link due to poor RF channel conditions. From a UE's perspective, this is a Radio Link Failure, and is referred to as Double S1 because when the UE performs TAU on the new eNB, the MME senses an existing S1 connection for the UE with the old serving eNB and thus sends UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND to release it.

4G|M8101C31.Updated: This counter is updated when UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND message is received from the MME with the cause value "Radio Connection with UE Lost", granted no UE CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST has been sent to the MME previously for a LTE-M UE.  This counter is only updated for Cat-M UEs working in CE ModeB.  Note: 'Double S1' in intra-LTE mobility context is resulted from a loss of radio link due to poor RF channel conditions. A connected UE can move over to another eNodeB without successfully requesting handover to the serving cell due to a sudden change in RF conditions. From UE's perspective, this is a Radio Link Failure. And it is referred to as double S1 because when the UE performs TAU on the new eNB, MME senses an existing S1 connection for the UE with the old serving eNB and thus sends CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND to release it.

4G|M8103C17.Network Element Name: PDCP time for successful transmissions in uplink (LTE-M)
4G|M8103C17.Network Element Name in previous release: PDCP time for successful transmissions in uplink (LTE-M)
4G|M8103C17.Description: This counter provides the total time after the data is received by the eNB from LTE-M UEs. The initial scheduling delay time is not counted. The counting is started when the first data transport block (TB) of a new burst has been received in the eNB, which means that the time between UL scheduling request (SR) and the first UL buffer status report (BSR) is not counted. In case the UE will send some data together with the first BSR, for this new burst, the counting is started at this point of time, and if not, then in the first regular sending of UL data via UL grant.  Note: The secondary narrowband is also taken into account.  Note: In case of TCP/IP traffic type with majority of the user data transmission in only one direction, the increased throughput may be observed in the opposite direction for which TCP ACK(s) were scheduled. This traffic cannot be distinguished by the eNB from the user data sent/received in the opposite direction and is strictly tied to TCP mechanism (error-check delivery).

4G|M8103C22.Network Element Name: PDCP time for successful transmissions in downlink (LTE-M)
4G|M8103C22.Network Element Name in previous release: PDCP time for successful transmissions in downlink (LTE-M)
4G|M8103C22.Description: This counter provides the total time after the data is sent to LTE-M UEs. This counter is used only for LTE-M UEs, which selected coverage enhancement level 1 at random access.  Note: The secondary narrowband is also taken into account.  Note: In case of TCP/IP traffic type with majority of the user data transmission in only one direction, the increased throughput may be observed in the opposite direction for which TCP ACK(s) were scheduled. This traffic cannot be distinguished by the eNB from the user data sent/received in the opposite direction and is strictly tied to TCP mechanism (error-check delivery).

4G|M8104C0.Network Element Name: Mean Value of the DL PRB utilization per TTI for Cat-M UEs served in CE ModeB
4G|M8104C0.Network Element Name in previous release: Mean Value of the DL PRB utilization per TTI for Cat-M UEs served in CE ModeB

4G|M8104C1.Network Element Name: Mean Value of the UL PRB utilization per TTI for Cat-M UEs served in CE ModeB
4G|M8104C1.Network Element Name in previous release: Mean Value of the UL PRB utilization per TTI for Cat-M UEs served in CE ModeB
4G|M8104C1.Description: This counter provides the mean value of the UL Physical Resource Block (PRB) utilization per TTI for Cat-M UEs served in CE ModeB.  The utilization is defined by the CE ModeB UL PRB ratio of the actual used (allocated) MPUSCH PRB number divided by the number of whole PRBs of UL bandwidth (e.g. 50 PRBs for 10MHz) per TTI. The MPUSCH PRBs of CE ModeB Msg3, Msg5, and the later UL initial and HARQ retransmission scheduling are counted, including MPUSCH repetitions, for both SRB/DRB. When no CE ModeB UE is scheduled on MPUSCH, the ratio is 0, except ghost scheduling. When LTE3561 is enabled, the ghost Msg3 is counted into the counter since ULPHY can’t distinguish NACK/DTX for CE ModeB;  When LTE3561 is disabled, the counter shall not be increased.  The reported value is 10 times higher than the actual value (for example 5.4 is stored as 54). This counter is used only for LTE-M.

This counter is incremented by each UL grant for which the eNB expects a Cat-M UE to use for the transmission of the DRB data. The actual received UL data is not considered for this counter.  Note: The eNB has to make certain assumptions depending on the cause for the allocated UL grants due to: - the LCG level UL BSR delivery (no bearer level accuracy) - the nature of the SR mechanism (no information about data type in buffer) - other uncertainties  These assumptions are listed below in detail:  This counter is incremented if the UL grant for the SR is assigned and if the eNB assumes that the DRB data will be sent. This is also true if the UE does not actually send any data using the assigned grant. This counter is also incremented in case of repetitions.  This counter is not incremented in case of: - the UL grant for the UE is reporting only LCG0 data transmission in UE buffers. This also applies in case QCI5 DRB is mapped to LCG0 - the UL grant is to a UE without the reception of a positive SR or without the reception of a BSR indication data in buffer (proactive UL scheduling) - the UL grant is for a scheduled UL transmission of an RA msg3/1st scheduled UL transmission after RA response/msg2 - the UL grant is for an SR if a UL SRB message is expected This counter is only updated for LTE-M UEs served in CE ModeB

4G|M8105C30.Description: This counter provides the number of times when user throughput in DL per burst is in the range from 0 to 127 kbit/s.  Note: In case of TCP/IP traffic type with majority of the user data transmission in only one direction, the increased throughput may be observed in the opposite direction for which TCP ACK(s) were scheduled. This traffic cannot be distinguished by the eNB from the user data sent/received in the opposite direction and is strictly tied to TCP mechanism (error-check delivery).

4G|M8105C30.Updated: This counter is updated each time the throughput (volume/time) value for the given burst falls into appropriate bin. The volume is calculated based on the successfully sent PDCP SDU per burst (SUCC_PDCP_VOL_DL_LTEM). The time is based on the difference between the first transmission TTI to the last transmission TTI (until the buffer is emptied) for each burst (SUCC_PDCP_TIME_DL_LTEM). Note: This counter is only updated for LTE-M UEs.

4G|M8200C52.Description: This counter provides the sum of sampled values for measuring the number of simultaneously RRC Connected NB-IoT UEs. Note: By a NB-IoT UE it is meant either a NB-IoT UE with a unique S-TMSI or a NB-IoT UE w/o S-TMSI.

4G|M8201C0.Network Element Name: Accumulated time duration in RRC_CONNECTED for NB-IoT UEs, which selected coverage enhancement level 0 during random access
4G|M8201C0.Network Element Name in previous release: Accumulated time duration in RRC_CONNECTED for NB-IoT UEs, which selected coverage enhancement level 0 during random access
4G|M8201C0.Description: This counter provides the total time of NB-IoT UEs, which selected coverage enhancement level 0 during random access, in RRC_CONNECTED state, that is, from the establishment of an RRC connection to its release.  Note: To obtain the average RRC connection time, this accumulated value should be divided by the number of RRC connections represented by the number of successful RRC connection setups (NB_IOT_RRC_CONN_CE0_SUM) or the number of RRC releases (sum of the respective releases counter values).
4G|M8201C0.Description in previous release: This counter provides the total time of NB-IoT UEs, which selected coverage enhancement level 0 during random access, in RRC_CONNECTED state, that is, from the establishment of an RRC connection to its release.  Note: To obtain the average RRC connection time, this accumulated value should be divided by the number of RRC connections represented by the number of successful RRC connection setups (NB_IOT_RRC_CONN_CE0_SUM) or the number of RRC releases (sum of the respective releases counter values).
4G|M8201C0.Updated: This counter is triggered when the first of three events (RLC ACK, HARQ ACK or timeout), as result of a started RRCConnectionRelease procedure, occurs. This counter is incremented by the time difference between this event and the corresponding RRCConnectionSetupComplete-NB message.  Note: only NB-IoT UEs, which selected coverage enhancement level 0 during random access, are to be considered.

4G|M8204C4.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of concurrently used NB-IoT non-anchor carriers in the UL, which are measured during an interval of one millisecond and accumulated over the measurement period.
4G|M8204C4.Updated: This counter is updated after each 1 ms interval, in which the UL resources on non-anchor carriers for the NB-IoT UEs were used. It is incremented by the number of subcarriers (granularity of 3.75 kHz) used in parallel by any NB-IoT UE (15 kHz subcarriers result in an increment of 4 per interval).  Note: In case of NB-IoT inband mode, this 1 ms interval corresponds to a subframe of the hosting WB cell, which is a subframe containing one or more host PRBs allocated to NB-IoT UEs. These PRBs are considered unusable from the host cell perspective.

4G|M8204C107.Network Element Name: Used NB-IoT resources on the UL anchor carrier
4G|M8204C107.Network Element Name in previous release: Used NB-IoT resources on the UL anchor carrier
4G|M8204C107.Description: This counter provides the number of used NB-IoT sub-carriers occupied by the uplink anchor carrier which are measured during a 1-millisecond interval and accumulated over the measurement period.
4G|M8204C107.Description in previous release: This counter provides the number of used NB-IoT sub-carriers occupied by the uplink anchor carrier which are measured during a 1-millisecond interval and accumulated over the measurement period.
4G|M8204C107.Updated: This counter is updated after each 1-ms interval in which UL resources for NB-IoT UEs were used. It is incremented by the number of subcarriers (granularity of 3.75 kHz) used in parallel by any NB-IoT UE. (15 kHz subcarriers result in an increment of 4 per interval). Note: In case of NB-IoT inband mode, this 1-ms interval corresponds to a subframe of the hosting WB cell, that is a subframe containing one or more host PRBs allocated to NB-IoT UEs. These PRBs are considered unusable from the host cell perspective.
